package.svelte: >=5.29 (the components use {@attach}); the peer range stays ^5.0.0
add: @mdi/js, when the app uses MDI icons
every package the app imports itself and used to get through v4 (luxon, lodash, date-fns, ...)

added: @likable-hair/svelte/tokens.css
@likable-hair/svelte/base.css
@likable-hair/svelte/v4-compat.css
@likable-hair/svelte/themes/*.css
@likable-hair/svelte/tailwind.css
@likable-hair/svelte/tailwind-preset

layers.app: @layer reset, theme, base, global, components, utilities;
layers.themeFile: @layer reset, theme, base, global.base, global.theme, global.components, components, utilities;

icons.transform: Drop the `mdi-` prefix and camelCase the rest with an `mdi` prefix (`mdi-chevron-down` → `mdiChevronDown`), import it from '@mdi/js' and pass it as an expression: `icon={mdiChevronDown}`.

exports.name: mediaQuery
exports.note: Same flags and widths, as a reactive object instead of a store: `$mediaQuery.xs` → `breakpoints.xs`, also `breakpoints.mAndDown` and the other `...AndDown` / `...AndUp`. The server counts as wide (`xl`) now.

exports.name: theme
exports.note: Exported again with the same name: `$theme.dark` keeps working (and `theme.dark` is reactive without `$`), `theme.mode` and `theme.name` are new. `$theme.active` and `$theme.colors` (the runtime colors API, broken in v4) are gone: colors are CSS tokens and themes.

exports.name: toggleTheme
exports.note: Same behaviour. The choice is saved only after `rememberAppearance()` (see `global-dark-mode`).

exports.name: setTheme
exports.note: `setTheme` still exists but sets a named design theme (`data-theme`). `setTheme("dark")` type-checks and activates a theme that does not exist: replace it with `setMode("dark")`.

exports.name: countriesList
exports.note: Only the ISO codes are in the library; names come from `countryName(code, locale)`.

exports.name: countriesOptions
exports.note: Returns `Item[]` with localized names, sorted by name.

exports.name: FilterBuilder
exports.note: Same name, same methods, same `toJson()` output (the contract with the backends: verified against v4 on the same calls). Bugs fixed, check code that relied on them: `where({ a: 1 })` (object form) did nothing in v4 and now adds a `kind: "object"` condition; `where(key, operator, undefined)` sent the operator as the value and is now skipped; `toJson()` and `modifiers` return copies (v4 `toJson()` returned the internal array, so pushing into it changed the builder); `hasWhereOnColumn` also looks inside groups and subqueries; `on(a, "=", "")` keeps the empty value. `where(callback)` still throws if the callback adds `orderBy`, `select` or `join`. New: `whereNotIn`, `orWhereNotIn`, `whereNotNull`, `orWhereNotNull` (Knex aliases of the `notWhere*` names), `whereBetween(key, [from, to])` (open ends), `clone()`, `FilterBuilder.fromJson(json)`, `orderBy(column)` with `asc` default, `toQueryParam()` (the whole query as one JSON string for a GET parameter, see `global-filter-backends`), exported types `JsonQuery`, `Modifier`, `WhereModifier`, `JoinModifier`, ... No lodash: `Date` values are cloned with `structuredClone` and still serialize as ISO UTC strings.

exports.name: FilterConverter
exports.note: The converter of v4 `Filter[]` is gone with the `Filter` type: definitions become `fields` and the applied state a `value` tree (see Filters, `filters-definitions` and `filters-initial-value`). `new FilterConverter().createBuilder({ filters })` → `filtersToBuilder(value, fields)`; to add the filters to an existing query (search, sort, tenant) pass it as `{ builder }`: it is copied, not changed, and the result has its joins first. Inside a Filters `onchange` the builder is already in the argument (`e.builder`): drop the call there. Also in load functions and server code (it has no DOM dependency). See `global-filter-converter`.

exports.name: Converter
exports.note: Same class as FilterConverter (v4 exported it twice): same migration.

exports.name: FilterValidator
exports.note: `FilterValidator.isValid(filter)` → `isConditionComplete(condition, field)`: whether a condition has a complete value for its operator (operators without a value, such as `empty` or `isTrue`, are always complete; a field can decide with `isComplete(condition)`; by default a custom value is complete when it is not `undefined`, `null`, `""`, an empty array or an empty object). Incomplete conditions are skipped by `filtersToBuilder` and by the count. `countFilters(value, fields)` counts the complete visible ones.

exports.name: DynamicFilters
exports.note: The master-detail list of DynamicTable (passed as Filters `contentSnippet`) is replaced by the Filters panel ("Filters" button: every condition in rows, with AND / OR and groups when allowed). Drop it together with `contentSnippet` and its `updateMultiFilterValues` / `updateCustomFilterValues` plumbing; custom inputs go in the Filters `inputSnippet`. Quick filters of the v4 tables (internal QuickFilters) become Filters `pinned` fields (always in the bar; "missing value" = operator `empty`, a three-state bool = `isTrue` / `isFalse` / no condition) and `presets` (chips that add ready conditions).

exports.name: HeaderMenu
exports.note: Not ported: no app used it. For a page with a top bar and a menu use SidebarLayout; for a bar alone write a `<header>` in the app with the library Button and Drawer.

exports.name: QuickActions
exports.note: Not ported: the floating bar of the selected rows is part of DataTable (`selectionActions`, `selectionActionsSnippet`).

exports.name: InfiniteScroll
exports.note: Not ported: Table calls `onendreached` when its last rows come into view, and DataTable has `pagination="infinite"`. Elsewhere use an `IntersectionObserver` on the last element.

exports.name: Navigator
exports.note: Not ported: it was the list of the v4 Drawer `items`. Put a HierarchyMenu (links with `currentPath`) or a TabSwitcher with `href` in the Drawer.

exports.name: Breadcrumb
exports.note: Not ported: no app used it. Write a `<nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">` with links in the app.

exports.name: VerticalSwitch
exports.note: Not ported: no app used it. Use Switch for a yes/no value, or TabSwitcher `variant="segmented"` with two tabs for two labelled choices.

exports.name: VerticalTextSwitch
exports.note: Not ported: no app used it. Use TabSwitcher `variant="segmented"` with two tabs.

exports.name: SelectableVerticalList
exports.note: Not ported: one app used it outside copied v4 filters. For a list where the user picks one entry use RadioGroup `card` (`title` → `label`, `name` → `value`, `description` and `icon` stay); for a list of results with the keyboard use Autocomplete or AsyncAutocomplete.

exports.name: SelectableMenuList
exports.note: Not ported: two apps used it, as a column of actions. Use HierarchyMenu with options without `href` and `onoptionClick` (`collapsed` → `iconsOnly`, `label` and `icon` stay), or a column of text Buttons.

exports.name: CollapsibleDivider
exports.note: Not ported: no app used it. Use a `<details>` with a Divider `label` in its `<summary>`.

exports.name: ColorInvertedSelector
exports.note: Not ported (it was the menu inside UnstableDividedSideBarLayout, used directly by one app); available on request. A list of options to choose from is a HierarchyMenu, or a TabSwitcher.

exports.name: SidebarMenuList
exports.note: Not ported (one app); available on request. HierarchyMenu with `href` on the options and `currentPath={page.url.pathname}` does what `autoDetectUrl` did; `title` → `label`, `url` → `href`, `children` → `options`.

exports.name: AvatarDropdown
exports.note: Not ported (one app); available on request.

exports.name: VerticalDraggableList
exports.note: Not ported (it was the list inside HeadersDrawer; three files in the apps); available on request.

exports.name: scrollAtCenter
exports.note: Not ported (one app): the browser does it.

exports.name: debounce
exports.note: Not ported (one app); available on request. A debounce is a few lines in the app (`clearTimeout` + `setTimeout`).

manual.summary: The components need Svelte 5.29 or later.
manual.action: Update `svelte` in the app before anything else (`setup` raises the range in `package.json`).

manual.summary: v5 has one runtime dependency (`flag-icons`); v4 brought 16.
manual.action: Run `svelte-check` and the build: every import that now fails to resolve (`luxon`, `lodash`, `date-fns`, ...) must be added to the app `package.json`.

manual.summary: All library CSS lives in cascade layers; unlayered app CSS always wins.
manual.action: Put the `layers.app` line at the top of the main app CSS, before any `@import`. Move global element resets (`button {}`, `input {}`, `* { margin: 0 }`, ...) into `@layer reset { ... }`, otherwise they restyle the inside of the components.

manual.summary: Tailwind 3 preflight removes component backgrounds and borders unless it is layered. `setup` wraps `@tailwind base;` in `@layer reset { ... }`, adds `presets: [aurora]` (`import aurora from '@likable-hair/svelte/tailwind-preset'`) to `tailwind.config.js` and turns `darkMode: 'class'` into the variant of the library.
manual.action: Token overrides placed in Tailwind's `@layer base` end up inside `reset` and lose: move them out of the layer.

manual.summary: Tailwind 4 needs the layer line and the library theme mapping.
manual.action: Put the `layers.app` line before `@import 'tailwindcss'`, then `@import '@likable-hair/svelte/tailwind.css'`. Note that it redefines `rounded-{xs,sm,md,lg,xl}`, `shadow-{sm,md,lg}`, `font-sans` and `font-mono`.

manual.summary: Internal class names changed (`.button`, `.chip`, `.textfield`, `.hint`, `.row`, `.overlay`, `._teleported`, `[data-dialog]` → `aurora-{component}-{part}` and `data-*`).
manual.action: Search app CSS for `:global(...)` selectors that target library internals and rewrite them against the v5 classes and `data-*` attributes, or replace them with CSS variables.

manual.summary: v4 color tokens (RGB triplets) do not exist in v5: overrides stop working and uses become undefined, unless the app imports `@likable-hair/svelte/v4-compat.css`.
manual.action: While migrating, import `@likable-hair/svelte/v4-compat.css` after the other imports of the app CSS (the migration tool does it): v4 names map to the Aurora colors and app overrides keep working and set the v5 brand colors. To finish, find `tokens.find` in app CSS and style attributes; replace each use following `tokens.mappings` by the role the color plays there (not by step number), and `rgb(var(...))` following `tokens.usage`. Remove `--global-color-light-*` / `--global-color-dark-*` overrides: set the v5 tokens with `light-dark()` instead, or use the `classic` theme.

manual.summary: Dark mode follows `color-scheme` and `data-mode` on `<html>`; `.dark` / `.light` classes do nothing. `setup` calls `rememberAppearance()` and `appearanceScript()` in the root layout (same `theme` key of v4, no flash) and changes Tailwind 3 `darkMode: 'class'`; the codemod renames `toggleTheme()` to `toggleMode()`.
manual.action: Replace `setTheme('dark')` with `setMode('dark')`, `.dark` selectors in app CSS with `[data-mode='dark']` plus the `prefers-color-scheme` branch (`@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { :root:not([data-mode='light']) ... }`), and a Tailwind 4 `@custom-variant dark` with the variant in MIGRATION.md. An app without dark mode sets `data-mode="light"` on `<html>`.

manual.summary: Every icon prop takes an SVG path; `"mdi-*"` strings type-check but draw nothing, and the global `.mdi` classes are gone.
manual.action: The codemod turns every `"mdi-*"` literal into an `@mdi/js` import (`icons.transform`), in attributes and in data. Left by hand: names built at runtime (`"mdi-" + name`: map them to the imported paths), and markup that uses `class="mdi mdi-*"` directly, which needs `@mdi/font` loaded by the app or an `<Icon path>` (while such markup exists the codemod converts only the icons of the library components).

manual.summary: Callbacks receive native events or plain objects instead of `{ detail: {...} }`.
manual.action: Apply `callbacks.argument` (or the component rule) to every callback of a library component, including handlers defined as functions elsewhere in the file and their TypeScript types (`CustomEvent<...>`, `ComponentProps<...>["onclick"]`).

manual.summary: Tokens name Geist, Bricolage Grotesque and Geist Mono; the library does not load them.
manual.action: Either load those fonts in the app or set `--global-font-family`, `--global-font-family-display` and `--global-font-family-mono` to the app fonts in an unlayered `:root` rule.

manual.summary: Dialog, Drawer and Menu use the top layer: the page is inert while a Dialog or Drawer is open, their content inherits from where it is written and unmounts when closed.
manual.action: Check app toasts, chat widgets and third-party popups that must work above an open Dialog. Move local state of Dialog/Drawer content into the parent. App Escape handlers should check `event.defaultPrevented`. Rules on `html { overflow }` defeat the scroll lock.

manual.summary: Required in every Italian app: without `setDefaultLocale('it')` the date and time fields read and write in English (MM/DD/YYYY, 12-hour clock), so a typed "05/03" is saved as May 3; in development they warn in the console. Texts and formats follow `locale` (BCP 47; Italian and English built in, other languages get the English texts): the `locale` prop of a component wins over `setDefaultLocale`, which wins over the default `en`. v4 was Italian by default in the date components (dd/MM/yyyy, Italian names, weeks from Monday) and in some texts ("Annulla" / "Salva", "N Selezionati"), and had `lang` props (default `en`) elsewhere.
manual.action: In the root `src/routes/+layout.svelte` of an Italian app, import `setDefaultLocale` from `@likable-hair/svelte` and call `setDefaultLocale('it')` in its `<script>`: it is a Svelte context (safe with SSR) that reaches every library component of the app, the Toaster and the content of dialogs included. With paraglide, follow the active language: `setDefaultLocale(() => getLocale())` (`getLocale` from `$lib/paraglide/runtime`). Then drop `locale="it"` where it only restored the Italian default and the Italian texts passed only to translate the English defaults (`invalidText`, `closeLabel`, `cancelText="Annulla"`, ...); v4 `lang="it"` becomes `locale="it"`, or nothing. Components that v4 showed in English without `lang` (Dropdown placeholder "Select", NoData "No data available", Filters, FilterEditor) become Italian: pass `locale="en"` where English is wanted. Text props passed by the app always win. Components rendered outside the layout (`mount()`, tests, a second root) need their own `setDefaultLocale` or `locale`.

manual.summary: v5 has toasts (`<Toaster />`, `addToast`, `addErrorToast`, `addSuccessToast`, `addWarningToast`, `addInfoToast`, `updateToast`, `removeToast`); most apps have their own `Toaster.svelte` copied from the melt-ui demo with the same function names but `{ data: { title, description, closeDelay, showLoading, action } }` arguments.
manual.action: Turn the app `Toaster.svelte` into the adapter shown in MIGRATION.md ("Toaster"), so call sites keep working: map `data.closeDelay` → `duration` (`0` now really keeps it open; default 5000), `data.showLoading` → `loading`, `data.action.handler` → `action.onclick`. Then check: `add*(...).id` → `add*(...)` (they return the id); CSS color strings (`color: "info"`, `"green"`) → the function or `variant`; remove-then-add loading flows → `updateToast(id, { variant: "success", title, loading: false })`; action handlers that must keep the toast open call `event.preventDefault()`. Remove the app melt-ui dependency once nothing else uses it.

manual.summary: Date components work with `Date` values at local midnight; `toISOString()` converts them to UTC and gives the previous day in Italy, and `new Date("yyyy-mm-dd")` reads the string as UTC midnight. v4 brought `luxon`, which apps used to convert these dates.
manual.action: Where a value bound to a date component is turned into a string, replace `date.toISOString()` (and `.toISOString().split('T')[0]`, `.slice(0, 10)`) with `toISODate(date)`, and where a `yyyy-mm-dd` string becomes the value, `new Date(text)` with `parseISODate(text)` (both from `@likable-hair/svelte`). luxon conversions (`DateTime.fromJSDate(d).toISODate()`, `DateTime.fromISO(s).toJSDate()`) are correct, but the app must declare `luxon` in its `package.json`.

manual.summary: v5 has a time field, `TimePickerTextField` (and the `TimePicker` panel); v4 had none, so apps wrap `<SimpleTextField type="time">` / `<StandardTextfield type="time">` or a bare `<input type="time">` in local components (`StandardTimePicker`, a local `TimePickerTextField`, `TimeField`).
manual.action: Find the local wrappers (`grep -rlE "type=\"time\"" src`, usually `$lib/components/common/StandardTimePicker.svelte`) and replace each usage with `<TimePickerTextField bind:value label=... name=... />` from `@likable-hair/svelte`; then delete the wrapper. The value stays a 24-hour `HH:mm` string (`HH:mm:ss` from a Postgres `time` column is read too, and the field writes back `HH:mm` only when the user changes it). Differences to check: (1) Italian apps get the 24-hour clock and the Italian texts from `setDefaultLocale("it")` in the root layout (step `global-default-locale`) or from `locale="it"` (the default `en` shows a 12-hour clock with AM/PM; the value is 24-hour anyway); (2) an empty field is `undefined`, not `""`: code that compares with `""` or sends `""` to the backend checks for both or uses `value ?? ""`; (3) `onchange` on the wrapper (often a bubbled native `change`) becomes `onchange({ value })`, called once per whole valid time, not at every key; `oninput` stays native; (4) wrapper props move to the field: `label`, `name` (hidden input with `HH:mm`), `required`, `disabled`, `placeholder`, `hint`, `state`, `min` / `max` as `HH:mm` (native `step` in seconds → `minuteStep` in minutes); (5) the wrapper CSS (`--simple-textfield-width`, borders, heights) becomes `--time-picker-text-field-*` or is dropped (the field is 100% wide). Wrappers that pair a date and a time (`StandardDateTimePicker`) become one `DateTimePickerTextField` (step `global-date-time-fields`).

manual.summary: v5 has a date and time field, `DateTimePickerTextField` (a `DatePicker` and a `TimePicker` in one panel, value `Date`); v4 had none, so apps pair a date field and a time field in local components (`StandardDateTimePicker` in likable-tools, addibox, lupette, epass, mufasa, evote; `StandardDateTimePickerTextfield` in stramoniumai).
manual.action: Find the wrappers (`grep -rlE "StandardDateTimePicker" src`, usually `$lib/components/common/StandardDateTimePicker.svelte`, which renders `StandardDatepicker` + `StandardTimePicker`) and replace each usage with `<DateTimePickerTextField bind:value label=... name=... />` from `@likable-hair/svelte` (plus `locale="it"` when the app has no `setDefaultLocale("it")`, step `global-default-locale`); then delete the wrapper. The value stays a `Date` with the local date and time (seconds at 0). Differences to check: (1) the wrappers default `value` to `new Date()` (now): the field starts empty, so where the old default mattered pass `value={new Date()}` (or a rounded time) explicitly; (2) an empty or invalid field is `undefined`; (3) `name` submits one hidden input with the local `yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm` instead of the date input (`name`) and the time input (`name + "-time"`): update the form action or the backend that read the two fields (`parseISODateTime(text)` reads it back); (4) `bind:value` keeps working, a bubbled `change` / `on:change` becomes `onchange({ value })`; stramoniumai's `selectedDateTime` / `menuOpened` become `bind:value` / `bind:open`, `error` → `state="error"`, `hint` stays; (5) wrapper props move to the field: `label`, `hint` (`info` in evote), `required`, `disabled`, `min` / `max` (instants, `Date`), `isDateDisabled`, `minuteStep`; (6) the two-column layout CSS of the wrapper (`.container { display: flex }`, widths) goes away: the field is one input, 100% wide; widths and borders become `--date-time-picker-text-field-*`; (7) Italian apps rely on `setDefaultLocale("it")` or pass `locale="it"` (the default `en` is MM/dd/yyyy with a 12-hour clock and English texts). Code that converts the value with `toISOString()` sends UTC: use `toISODateTime(date)` for a local `yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm`, or keep `toISOString()` where the backend expects an instant.

manual.summary: `FilterConverter` / `Converter` and the v4 `Filter` type are gone; queries come from `filtersToBuilder(value, fields, { builder })`.
manual.action: Search the app (components, stores, `+page.ts`, `+page.server.ts`, `+server.ts`, utils) for `FilterConverter`, `Converter`, `createBuilder(` and `Filter[]`. Where the filters come from a Filters component, use the `builder` of its `onchange` and delete the conversion. Elsewhere (first load, SSR, exports, jobs, saved filters) convert the definitions to `fields` and the state to a tree (Filters rule, `filters-definitions` / `filters-initial-value`) and call `filtersToBuilder(value, fields)`; when the code then added more conditions to the returned builder (search, tenant, sorting), build those first and pass them as `{ builder }`, or keep adding them to the result. Keep `fields` in one module shared by the page and the load function.

manual.summary: The filters can now send `kind: "in"` for selects, OR groups and nested groups, `yyyy-MM-dd` strings for dates, Postgres regex and array operators, and the kinds `null`, `column`, `inBuilder`, `jsonSuperset` and `raw` (JSON keys with `cast`); the backends (`FilterModifierApplier`, not in this repo) replay them with different fidelity.
manual.action: Check the backend of the app before turning features on. (1) Select fields with one value send `where(column, "=", v)` (`notIn`: `"<>"`), with several values `{ method: "where", kind: "in", key, value: [...] }` (`notIn`: `logicalOperator: "andNot"`), instead of a group of `orWhere` (v4 `equal`) or of `whereNot` (v4 `different`): every applier handles `in`, and it fixes the select OR of lupette and likable-tools, whose appliers flatten groups. (2) `allowOr` and `maxDepth` are off by default (AND only, as v4); turn them on only where the applier replays `grouped` with its `logicalOperator` at every level: variant A (astro, ermes, h24, maya, quantum, cbam) is fine; B (biblio, biblio-smart-folder, contattorapido, tatum, addibox, stramoniumai) applies OR only inside a group, which is how Filters sends it; C (billboards, mufasa, emarket) and E' (epass, new-vigipass) join groups with AND; D (ganymede) reads one level; E (lupette, likable-tools) flattens groups. With OR at the root every condition goes inside one `grouped`, so managers that read first-level modifiers by key (astro, cbam, ganymede, maya, lupette, quantum, stramoniumai) stop seeing them. (3) GET requests: Adonis parses the query string with `qs` at depth 5 and `arrayLimit` 20, and no app raises them. Anything deeper than `filtersBuilder[modifiers][i][children][j][key]` is silently mangled: arrays inside a group or a subquery become `{ "[0]": ... }` (a select with 2+ values inside an OR group, a `through` field with 2+ values, `whereIn` with a callback and an array inside), a group inside a group loses its children; arrays with more than 20 items become objects (v4 selects had the same limit). `qs` turns numbers and booleans into strings, also inside objects (a `json` field without `cast` sends `whereJsonSuperset(column, { visits: 5 })`, which arrives as `{ visits: "5" }` and no longer matches a JSON number). Fix, in order of preference: send `filtersBuilder: builder.toQueryParam()` (the whole query as one JSON string) and change the backend line that reads it to `typeof input === "string" ? JSON.parse(input) : input` (it keeps accepting the old format); or raise `http.qs.parse.depth` and `arrayLimit` in the backend `config/app.ts`; or send `builder.toJson()` in a POST body. (4) Date fields with `dateOnly: true` send `yyyy-MM-dd` strings instead of `Date` (ISO UTC timestamps): set it only on `date` columns. (5) `contains` sends `ilike` with `%v%` and escapes `%`, `_` and `\`; appliers A–E wrap like/ilike values in `%` again (same results), E' does not. They add `%` only when the operator is exactly `like` or `ilike`, so the other text operators reach Postgres unchanged on every applier (all use `pg`): `notContains` (`not ilike "%v%"`, `not like` with `caseSensitive`), `startsWith` / `endsWith` (regex `~*`, or `~` with `caseSensitive`, value `^v` / `v$` with the regex characters escaped), `is` / `isNot` / `anyOf` / `noneOf` (regex `~*` / `!~*` on `^v$` or `^(a|b)$`, so they ignore case; `=` / `<>` / `in` with `caseSensitive`, as v4), `is` / `isNot` with `words` (`~*` / `!~*` on `\mword\M`). (6) Sorting added by a field `apply` (`orderBy`) comes after the conditions in the modifiers, as before. (7) Kinds: A–D replay `null`, `column`, `jsonSuperset` and `inBuilder`; E (lupette, likable-tools) and E' (epass, new-vigipass) know only `simple`, `object`, `grouped` and `in`, and throw "where kind not supported" (a 500) for `empty` / `notEmpty` (`whereNull`, also string `empty` with `blankIsEmpty`), `compareWith` and `whenTrue` / `whenFalse` with `whereColumn` (`column`), `through` (`inBuilder`) and `json`. On those apps pass `negativesIncludeEmpty={false}` (on by default, it adds `whereNull` to every negative operator) and `operatorSet="basic"` to Filters (the default `standard` set has `empty` / `notEmpty`), or `typeOperators` / field `operators` without them, and avoid those options; or add the missing branches to the applier (copy them from variant A). (8) Select fields with `array: true` send `where(column, "&&", [...])` (`in`), `"@>"` (`all`), `whereNot(column, "&&", [...])` (`notIn`), `whereNull` or `= "{}"` (`empty`, the empty array as a Postgres literal, so GET requests keep it): Postgres array operators as simple wheres, replayed by every applier that knows `null`. (9) `json` fields without `cast` send `kind: "jsonSuperset"` (A–D; negations inside a `whereNot` group). With `cast` they send `kind: "raw"`, clause `(??#>>?)::<cast> <operator> ?` with bindings `[column, "{key,path}", value]`: only B replays `raw` (A, C, D throw "where kind not supported"). Relying on `raw`, in B or by adding it elsewhere, means the server runs whatever SQL condition a client sends (the clause is not checked server side): prefer accepting `raw` only for whitelisted columns and that exact clause shape, or expose the key as a real column or a view. Security, outside the library: the appliers accept any column, table and subquery from the client (and B passes `kind: "raw"` to `whereRaw`); a whitelist per manager is recommended.

manual.summary: Filter state saved by the app (stores, sessionStorage / localStorage, URL presets, load functions) was a v4 `Filter[]` rebuilt by hand; in v5 it is the `value` tree, plain JSON.
manual.action: Store `serializeFilters(value)` (a JSON string) and restore with `parseFilters(json, fields)`, which drops conditions on unknown fields and returns an empty tree for invalid input: replaces the stores that survived navigation, the session storage copies and the code that re-applied `active` / `value` to each definition. URL: `filtersToParam(value)` is the same tree without the node identities (shorter): write `?filters=${encodeURIComponent(filtersToParam(value))}` into the URL (links, `replaceState`, or `goto` when the load function fetches the data), and read it with `filtersFromParam(url.searchParams.get("filters"), fields)` in the load function (new identities, unknown fields dropped, empty tree for missing or invalid input). URL presets made of separate parameters → build the tree there (`createFilters([filterCondition("status", "in", [{ value: url.searchParams.get("status"), label: ... }])])`). In both cases compute the first query in the load function with `filtersToBuilder(value, fields)` and pass `value` to the page for `bind:value`. Named sets of filters the app kept itself (saved views, favourite searches; v4 had no such feature) → Filters `savable` (kept in memory), `savedKey="<page>-filters"` (kept in `localStorage`) or `bind:saved` / `onsavedchange` (a `SavedFilter[]` of `{ id, name, value }` to store in the backend). Saved sets and URL parameters carry the whole tree, `locked` conditions included, and applying a saved set replaces the conditions: keep constraints the user must not change (tenant, permissions) in the `builder` prop or in the backend, not only in locked conditions. Saved trees keep working when fields are added; rename a field `name` only with a conversion of the saved trees. Saved v4 `Filter[]` cannot be read by `parseFilters`: convert them once or drop them.

manual.summary: `items` are now suggestions shown while the text is shorter than `searchThreshold`, filtered locally; the results of `searcher` no longer overwrite them. v4 kept showing the last results, unfiltered, below the threshold.
manual.action: Where `items` held initial results, keep them as suggestions or use `searchThreshold={0}`, which runs `searcher` with an empty text as soon as the list opens. Without `items` the list asks to "Type at least N characters" (`thresholdText`).

manual.summary: `searcher` receives an `AbortSignal` and runs only while the list is open: opening it with enough text searches at once, reopening with the same text reuses the last results, and `searching` is `true` while a search waits for the debounce or runs, that is once the trimmed text reaches `searchThreshold` with the list open (or after `search()`).
manual.action: Pass `signal` to `fetch` and remove app-side debounce, request counters or "ignore stale response" guards. Code that set `searchText` from outside and expected a search must open the list or call `search()`.

manual.summary: A rejected `searcher` shows an error row ("Couldn't load results") and calls `onerror(error)`; searches aborted by a newer one or by unmounting the component are not errors. v4 left an unhandled rejection.
manual.action: Move error toasts or logging from `try/catch` inside `searcher` to `onerror`, and let the error propagate (rethrow) so the row shows. Customize with `errorText` or `errorSnippet({ error, search })`.

manual.summary: While searching, the field shows a spinner and the list three skeleton rows (with a hidden "Loading…" text); Enter picks nothing until the results arrive.
manual.action: Remove app loading indicators placed next to the field; restyle the rows with `--async-autocomplete-skeleton-*` or replace them with `loadingSnippet`.

manual.summary: `Item.icon` is an SVG path (v4: an MDI class name; the codemod converts the `"mdi-*"` literals) and `Item` is exported from the package root.
manual.action: Import `type Item` from `@likable-hair/svelte` instead of the component module; with TypeScript, `Item` without a type argument now has `data: unknown`, so pass the type (`Item<{ price: number }>`) where the app reads `item.data`.

manual.summary: Values are compared with `===` (v4 mixed `==` and `===`) and duplicate `value`s in `items` or `values` throw.
manual.action: Check that `values` use the same type as `items` (`{ value: 1 }` and `{ value: "1" }` are different options now: ids read from the URL or a form are strings) and that `items` has no duplicate `value`.

manual.summary: It is an ARIA combobox: the focus stays in the input and options are not tab stops (neither is the v4 wrapper). While typing, the first match is highlighted and Enter picks it without submitting the form; Backspace on an empty field removes the last value; Escape closes the list and keeps the focus; the arrows do not move the caret.
manual.action: Check forms where Enter in the field was expected to submit while an option is highlighted, and end-to-end tests that tabbed into the options or clicked the wrapper; use `getByRole("combobox")` and `getByRole("option")`.

manual.summary: `closeOnSelect={true}` now also closes the list with `multiple` (v4 ignored it there).
manual.action: Remove `closeOnSelect` from `multiple` usages that must keep the list open.

manual.summary: `searchText` keeps its initial value (v4 erased it after mount) and becomes `""` (not `undefined`) when the list closes.
manual.action: Replace checks like `searchText === undefined` with `!searchText`.

manual.summary: With single selection, picking another option calls `onchange` with the replaced value in `unselect` as well as the new one in `select`.
manual.action: Check handlers that treat `unselect` as "the user cleared the field": test `select === undefined` (or `selection.length === 0`) instead.

manual.summary: `disabled` disables the native input: it gets no focus, the list does not open and chips have no remove button. With `mandatory` the last chip has no remove button either.
manual.action: Check flows that relied on focusing or opening a disabled Autocomplete (v4 only faded it).

manual.summary: With `mobileDrawer`, on screens up to 1024px the list opens in a bottom drawer that has its own search field and a title (`drawerTitle ?? label`); the field on the page becomes read-only. v4 showed only the list. The server renders the desktop variant.
manual.action: Pass `label` or `drawerTitle` so the drawer has a title; pass `drawerSearch={false}` for short lists that need no search.

manual.summary: `itemSnippet` replaces the content of an option, not the option: the row keeps its click handling, `role="option"`, the selected and highlighted states and their styles.
manual.action: Remove from the snippet the wrapper that drew the row (click handlers, padding, selected or focused backgrounds) and keep only the content; use `selected` and `highlighted` from the parameters for content that changes with the state.

manual.summary: `itemLabelSnippet` replaces only the label: the `item.icon` and the check mark of selected options stay (v4 dropped the icon).
manual.action: If the snippet drew the icon itself, remove it from the snippet or move it to `itemIconSnippet`.

manual.summary: `hintSnippet` renders inside the hint element (linked to the input with `aria-describedby`) instead of in place of it.
manual.action: Remove wrappers or margins the snippet added to position itself under the field.

manual.summary: New look: the field uses the `--global-input-*` base (36px minimum height, input border and focus ring), takes 100% of the container width, chips are primary `sm` Chips, the selected options are tinted with a check mark (v4: filled primary) and the list is as wide as the field, at most 300px high.
manual.action: Check layouts where an Autocomplete sat in a row next to other elements: set `--autocomplete-width` (a length or `auto`) or size its container. Drop `--chip-*` overrides that targeted the v4 chips if they now look wrong.

removed.name: menuWidth
removed.note: The list is always as wide as the field. To make it wider or narrower set `--menu-min-width` / `--menu-max-width` on the Autocomplete (`--menu-width` has no effect because the width is written inline).

removed.name: menuBoxShadow
removed.note: Set the Menu variable on the Autocomplete. The default v4 shadow used a v4 color token: drop it unless the app really wants a custom shadow.

removed.name: menuBorderRadius
removed.note: Set the Menu variable on the Autocomplete.

toCssVar.name: width
toCssVar.note: The default is now `100%` of the container (v4: `auto`, at least 200px). `width` still type-checks (it is an `<input>` attribute) but no longer sizes the component.

toCssVar.name: menuMaxHeight
toCssVar.note: Same default, `300px`.

defaults.name: placement
defaults.note: Visible only when the list is wider than the field (`--menu-min-width`).

values.name: placement
values.note: For values that came from `menuAnchor`. `"bottom"`, `"left"` and `"right"` still type-check but now mean centered.

types.name: searchFunction
types.note: Called only while `searchText` is not empty. The default search now ignores accents and matches `label ?? value`: a custom function that only did that can be dropped.

types.name: items
types.note: `Item` is exported from the package root (`import { type Item } from "@likable-hair/svelte"`), its `Data` defaults to `unknown` and `icon` is an SVG path.

types.name: values
types.note: Same `Item` type change as `items`.

types.name: class
types.v4: { activator?: string; menu?: string; simpleTextfield?: ...; hint?: string }
types.v5: { container?, label?, field?, input?, chip?, menu?, option?, hint?: string }
types.note: `activator` → `container` (whole component) or `field` (the bordered box). `menu` is now on the Menu element, not on the `<ul>` inside it. `simpleTextfield` had no effect: drop it. `hint` is on the hint element itself.

changed.name: onchange
changed.type: { select?: Item<Data>; unselect?: Item<Data>; selection: Item<Data>[] }
changed.note: With single selection, picking another option now reports the replaced one in `unselect` (v4: `undefined`).

changed.name: onfocus
changed.note: Native event of the input; v4 passed no argument.

changed.name: onblur
changed.note: Native event of the input; v4 passed no argument.

changed.name: onkeydown
changed.note: Native event of the input, as in v4. Calling `preventDefault()` in it now skips the built-in key handling (arrows, Enter, Backspace, Escape).

changed.name: onclose
changed.note: Fires on every close of the list; v4 fired it only when the mobile drawer closed.

removed.name: menuSnippet
removed.note: It replaced the whole list without parameters. Use `itemSnippet` / `itemLabelSnippet` / `itemIconSnippet` / `itemAppendSnippet` for the options, `loadingSnippet` and `emptySnippet` for the status rows, `--menu-*` and `--autocomplete-option-*` for the look.

parameters.name: itemSnippet
parameters.note: It now replaces the content of the option, not the option: see the manual step.

parameters.name: selectionContainerSnippet
parameters.v4: { values, searchText, disabled, openMenu, handleKeyDown, unselect, select }
parameters.v5: { values, searchText, disabled, openMenu, handleKeyDown, unselect, select, attributes }
parameters.note: Spread `attributes` (combobox role and ARIA state) on the focusable element of the custom trigger and call `handleKeyDown` from its `onkeydown`.

removed.note: Split in two variables.

removed.name: --autocomplete-default-border
removed.note: Split in two variables (v4 read it but never defined it).

removed.name: --autocomplete-focus-box-shadow
removed.note: Focus is a ring of fixed shape now.

removed.name: --autocomplete-default-focus-box-shadow
removed.note: Focus is a ring of fixed shape now.

removed.name: --autocomplete-options-max-width
removed.note: Options are as wide as the list and their labels wrap. Drop the override; to size the list use `--menu-min-width` / `--menu-max-width`.

removed.name: --autocomplete-default-options-max-width
removed.note: Options are as wide as the list and their labels wrap. Drop the override; to size the list use `--menu-min-width` / `--menu-max-width`.

removed.note: The hint is aligned with the field. Drop the override, or use `class.hint` with app CSS.

removed.name: --autocomplete-default-hint-margin-left
removed.note: The hint is aligned with the field. Drop the override, or use `class.hint` with app CSS.

manual.summary: `Item.icon` is an SVG path (v4: an MDI class name; the codemod converts the `"mdi-*"` literals) and `Item` is exported from the package root.
manual.action: Import `type Item` from `@likable-hair/svelte` instead of the component module; with TypeScript, `Item` without a type argument now has `data: unknown`, so pass the type (`Item<{ price: number }>`) where the app reads `item.data`.

manual.summary: Values are compared with `===` (v4 mixed `==` and `===`) and duplicate `value`s in `items` or `values` throw.
manual.action: Check that `values` use the same type as `items` (`{ value: 1 }` and `{ value: "1" }` are different options now: ids read from the URL or a form are strings) and that `items` has no duplicate `value`.

manual.summary: It is an ARIA combobox: the focus stays in the input and options are not tab stops (neither is the v4 wrapper). While typing, the first match is highlighted and Enter picks it without submitting the form; Backspace on an empty field removes the last value; Escape closes the list and keeps the focus; the arrows do not move the caret.
manual.action: Check forms where Enter in the field was expected to submit while an option is highlighted, and end-to-end tests that tabbed into the options or clicked the wrapper; use `getByRole("combobox")` and `getByRole("option")`.

manual.summary: `closeOnSelect={true}` now also closes the list with `multiple` (v4 ignored it there).
manual.action: Remove `closeOnSelect` from `multiple` usages that must keep the list open.

manual.summary: `searchText` keeps its initial value (v4 erased it after mount) and becomes `""` (not `undefined`) when the list closes.
manual.action: Replace checks like `searchText === undefined` with `!searchText`.

manual.summary: With single selection, picking another option calls `onchange` with the replaced value in `unselect` as well as the new one in `select`.
manual.action: Check handlers that treat `unselect` as "the user cleared the field": test `select === undefined` (or `selection.length === 0`) instead.

manual.summary: `disabled` disables the native input: it gets no focus, the list does not open and chips have no remove button. With `mandatory` the last chip has no remove button either.
manual.action: Check flows that relied on focusing or opening a disabled Autocomplete (v4 only faded it).

manual.summary: With `mobileDrawer`, on screens up to 1024px the list opens in a bottom drawer that has its own search field and a title (`drawerTitle ?? label`); the field on the page becomes read-only. v4 showed only the list. The server renders the desktop variant.
manual.action: Pass `label` or `drawerTitle` so the drawer has a title; pass `drawerSearch={false}` for short lists that need no search.

manual.summary: `itemSnippet` replaces the content of an option, not the option: the row keeps its click handling, `role="option"`, the selected and highlighted states and their styles.
manual.action: Remove from the snippet the wrapper that drew the row (click handlers, padding, selected or focused backgrounds) and keep only the content; use `selected` and `highlighted` from the parameters for content that changes with the state.

manual.summary: `itemLabelSnippet` replaces only the label: the `item.icon` and the check mark of selected options stay (v4 dropped the icon).
manual.action: If the snippet drew the icon itself, remove it from the snippet or move it to `itemIconSnippet`.

manual.summary: `hintSnippet` renders inside the hint element (linked to the input with `aria-describedby`) instead of in place of it.
manual.action: Remove wrappers or margins the snippet added to position itself under the field.

manual.summary: New look: the field uses the `--global-input-*` base (36px minimum height, input border and focus ring), takes 100% of the container width, chips are primary `sm` Chips, the selected options are tinted with a check mark (v4: filled primary) and the list is as wide as the field, at most 300px high.
manual.action: Check layouts where an Autocomplete sat in a row next to other elements: set `--autocomplete-width` (a length or `auto`) or size its container. Drop `--chip-*` overrides that targeted the v4 chips if they now look wrong.

manual.summary: Internal classes changed: `.selection-container` → `.aurora-autocomplete-field`, `.autocomplete-input` → `.aurora-autocomplete-field input`, `.selection-item` → `.aurora-autocomplete-option`, `.focused` → `[data-highlighted]`, `.selected` → `[data-selected]`, `.not-visible-chip-number` → `.aurora-autocomplete-counter`, `.hint` → `.aurora-autocomplete-hint`, `li.item-N` → `[role="option"]`.
manual.action: Rewrite app `:global(...)` selectors that target them, or replace them with `--autocomplete-*` variables.

added: `label` (linked to the input), `labelSnippet`, `id`.
`state` (`error` | `success`) with `stateIconSnippet`; `error` sets `aria-invalid`.
`name`: a hidden input per selected value, submitted with the form.
`icon` and `iconSnippet` at the start of the field.
`loading` with `loadingText` / `loadingSnippet`; `noResultsText` / `emptySnippet({ searchText })` when nothing matches.
`removeLabel` (chip remove buttons), `drawerSearch`, `drawerTitle`, `closeLabel` (mobile drawer).
`locale` (BCP 47): language of the default texts, Italian with `it`, English otherwise; without it the one of `setDefaultLocale` (step `global-default-locale`), else `en`. Text props win over it.
`chipIconSnippet`, `itemIconSnippet`, `itemAppendSnippet`.
`bind:input` and the native attributes and events of the `<input>`.
`data-state`, `data-disabled`, `data-open`, `data-loading` on the root element.
`--autocomplete-*` variables for the label, chips gap, counter, spinner, options, match highlight, status rows and drawer.

changed.name: alt
changed.note: v4: `alt` of the ``, `""` by default, so the avatar was always decorative. v5: accessible name of the whole avatar (role `img`), by default `name`; `alt=""` keeps it decorative. Without `name` nothing changes.

changed.name: imageLoadingStatus
changed.note: Gains `'loading'` (until the image arrives) and is `undefined` without `src`; v4 started at `'success'`. Code that tests `=== 'success'` to decide whether an image exists keeps working once the image has loaded.

changed.name: src
changed.note: Also accepts a `Blob` or `File`: the avatar creates and revokes the object URL. An empty string counts as no image, as before.

renamed.note: The avatar is always square: one size for width and height. Use a `size` (`xs` 24, `sm` 32, `md` 40, `lg` 56, `xl` 80) when the v4 value is one of those, else `--avatar-size`. If `--avatar-height` is also set, keep one of the two (`avatar-size`).
See `--avatar-width`: keep one of the two.
By default the text is 0.38 × the size (v4 about 0.41 × the height); set it only where a different ratio is wanted.

removed.name: --avatar-min-width
removed.note: The avatar no longer shrinks in a flex row (`flex-shrink: 0`), which is what the apps used it for: delete it.

removed.name: --avatar-max-width
removed.note: The size is fixed: delete it, or set `--avatar-size`.

removed.name: --avatar-min-height
removed.note: The size is fixed: delete it, or set `--avatar-size`.

removed.name: --avatar-max-height
removed.note: The size is fixed: delete it, or set `--avatar-size`.

removed.name: --avatar-default-min-width
removed.note: Never read by v4 either (set in some apps by mistake): delete it.

removed.name: --avatar-default-background-color
removed.note: The background is one of six gradients picked from the name (`--avatar-default-background-1` … `-6`, built on the `--global-color-data-*` tokens). For one color everywhere set `--avatar-background` in the app CSS, or `color="primary"` on the avatars.

removed.name: --avatar-default-text-color
removed.note: Text on the gradients is `--avatar-default-color`; on `color="neutral"` it is `--avatar-default-neutral-color`.

manual.summary: v5 computes the initials from `name`: first letter of the first and of the last word ("Mario Rossi" → "MR"). The apps passed `text={username.substring(0, 2).toUpperCase()}` ("MA").
manual.action: Replace `text={fullName.substring(0, 2).toUpperCase()}` (and similar code that builds initials) with `name={fullName}`, which also gives the color and the accessible name. Keep `text` only for text that is not initials, such as a short company name. Guard names that may be missing ("undefined undefined") before passing them.

manual.summary: The background is a gradient picked from the name, so every person has their own color; v4 used the primary color for everyone.
manual.action: Leave it where avatars stand for people. Pass `colorKey={id}` where the name can change but the color should not, `color="primary"` where the brand color must stay, and delete the per-person palettes built in the app (by position or by `id % n`).

manual.summary: `children` now replaces only the content inside the circle (initials or icon); in v4 it replaced the whole avatar, circle included.
manual.action: Where `children` rebuilt the circle (a `div` with the avatar size, radius and background around an icon), keep only the inner content, for example `<Avatar color={4}><Icon path={mdiCurrencyEur} /></Avatar>`.

manual.summary: Without `src`, `name` or `text` the avatar shows a person icon; v4 showed an empty circle.
manual.action: Nothing to do unless the empty circle was meant: pass `icon` for another icon, or `text=" "` for an empty avatar.

manual.summary: Default look: 40px circle (unchanged), text weight 600 instead of 700, text 0.38 × the size. The image covers the initials, which stay visible while it loads or when it fails (v4 showed the broken image for a moment and downloaded it twice).
manual.action: Compare the screens with avatars; restore `--avatar-font-weight="700"` where the bolder text is wanted. Where width and height differed (a rectangle), choose one size: rectangular avatars are not supported.

manual.summary: `src` accepts a `Blob`/`File`: images downloaded with authentication no longer need to be turned into data URLs.
manual.action: Where the app downloads the image as a blob and converts it with `FileReader.readAsDataURL` (or keeps an object URL it never revokes), pass the blob directly: `src={blob}`.

added: `name`: initials, color and accessible name.
`colorKey` and `color` (`auto`, `1`–`6`, `primary`, `neutral`): the background.
`size` (`xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`) and `--avatar-size`.
`shape="square"`, `ring`, `status` with `statusLabel`, `icon`, `locale`.
`badgeSnippet`: content in the bottom-right corner.
`class`, native attributes and `avatarElement` on the root `<span>`.
`--avatar-gap-color`, `--avatar-ring-color`, `--avatar-ring-width`, `--avatar-status-color`, `--avatar-status-size`.
`AvatarGroup`: overlapping avatars with a "+N" counter.

changed.name: data
changed.note: Same shape as the chart.js `data`: `{ labels, datasets }`, and chart.js dataset keys still work. Svelte state can be passed as it is: remove `$state.snapshot(...)`. New library keys per series: `color` (any CSS color, also `var(--…)`; an array gives one color per bar) instead of `backgroundColor`/`borderColor`, `type: 'line'` with `axis: 'right'` instead of `yAxisID` and a scale of its own, `format` for the values of that series. Keys that only repeated the old defaults are no longer needed: `tension`, `fill: false`, `borderWidth`, `borderRadius`, `maxBarThickness`.

changed.name: options
changed.note: Still chart.js options, merged over the defaults of the library (no longer mutated). The common ones are props now (`horizontal`, `stacked`, `format`, `legend`, `zoom`): see the `-options` step. Optional in v5.

changed.name: width
changed.note: Native attributes (`width`, `height`, `class`, `style`, `id`) go to the root `<div>`, no longer to the `<canvas>`. Size the chart with `--bar-chart-width` / `--bar-chart-height` (same names with `line-chart` and `pie-chart`).

removed.name: resetZoom
removed.note: While zoomed the chart shows its own "Reset zoom" icon in the top-right corner of the plot, and a double click also resets. Remove `bind:resetZoom` and the reset button of the app. To reset from code, `bind:chart` and call `chart.resetZoom()`.

removed.name: showXTicks
removed.note: A prop of the v3 charts that did nothing in v4 (it ended up as an attribute of the canvas): the chart keeps its look. Ticks are visible and the legend shows with two or more series by default.

removed.name: showYTicks
removed.note: A prop of the v3 charts that did nothing in v4 (it ended up as an attribute of the canvas): the chart keeps its look. Ticks are visible and the legend shows with two or more series by default.

removed.name: pointRadius
removed.note: A prop of the v3 charts that did nothing in v4 (it ended up as an attribute of the canvas): the chart keeps its look. Ticks are visible and the legend shows with two or more series by default.

removed.name: showLegend
removed.note: A prop of the v3 charts that did nothing in v4 (it ended up as an attribute of the canvas): the chart keeps its look. Ticks are visible and the legend shows with two or more series by default.

removed.name: rgbTooltipColor
removed.note: A prop of the v3 charts that did nothing in v4 (it ended up as an attribute of the canvas): the chart keeps its look. Ticks are visible and the legend shows with two or more series by default.

removed.name: rgbTooltipBackgroundColor
removed.note: A prop of the v3 charts that did nothing in v4 (it ended up as an attribute of the canvas): the chart keeps its look. Ticks are visible and the legend shows with two or more series by default.

removed.name: tooltipLabel
removed.note: A prop of the v3 charts that did nothing in v4 (it ended up as an attribute of the canvas): the chart keeps its look. Ticks are visible and the legend shows with two or more series by default.

removed.name: displayYGrid
removed.note: A prop of the v3 charts that did nothing in v4 (it ended up as an attribute of the canvas): the chart keeps its look. Ticks are visible and the legend shows with two or more series by default.

removed.name: displayXGrid
removed.note: A prop of the v3 charts that did nothing in v4 (it ended up as an attribute of the canvas): the chart keeps its look. Ticks are visible and the legend shows with two or more series by default.

manual.summary: `$state.snapshot(...)` around `data` is no longer needed: the chart copies the values itself.
manual.action: Pass the `$state` / `$derived` data directly: `data={$state.snapshot(chartData)}` → `data={chartData}`.

manual.summary: Colors follow the theme and dark mode by themselves: the code that read the v4 tokens by hand for the canvas is no longer needed.
manual.action: Look in the component for `getComputedStyle(...).getPropertyValue('--global-color-…')`, `readToken`, `rgb(${...})` strings built from the v4 triplets, effects or `if ($theme.dark)` that exist only to recolor the chart, and `hsl(i * N, …)` palettes. Remove them: series without `color` take the data palette of the theme (`--global-color-data-1…6`, one series alone gets the brand gradient); where a specific color matters, write `color: 'var(--global-color-…)'` with the v5 token of the same role (see Color tokens in MIGRATION.md). One color per bar: an array in `color`.

manual.summary: Props of the v3 charts (`xTickLabel`, `enableZoom`, `yMin`, …) did nothing in v4: they ended up as attributes of the canvas, so the chart was drawn with the defaults. The codemod removes the ones with nothing to keep (`showXTicks`, `pointRadius`, `rgbTooltipColor`, …).
manual.action: Delete them, or give them the meaning the app wanted: `enableZoom` → `zoom` (`zoom={false}` turns zooming off, which v4 never did); `xTickLabel`/`yTickLabel` that format numbers → `format`; `xMin`/`xMax`/`yMin`/`yMax` → `options={{ scales: { y: { min, max } } }}`. `horizontal` is a prop again and keeps working.

manual.summary: Global chart.js tweaks of the app (`Chart.defaults.…`, `Chart.register(...)` of an app plugin) were made for the v4 charts.
manual.action: Remove `Chart.defaults.resizeDelay` and plugins registered only to fix the hover of horizontal bars (`interaction.axis` follows `horizontal` now). Keep the app’s own chart.js charts, if any, as they are.

manual.summary: Most `options` the apps pass are props or defaults now; what is left stays in `options`.
manual.action: Move and delete, then keep in `options` only what is left: `maintainAspectRatio: false` → delete (the chart fills `--bar-chart-height`, 16rem; write `--bar-chart-height="100%"` to fill a widget that has a height); `scales.*.ticks.display: true` → delete (visible by default); `ticks.callback: (v, i) => labels[i]` → delete; tick and tooltip callbacks that only format numbers (`toLocaleString`, `Intl.NumberFormat`, `€`, `%`) → `format` (options of `Intl.NumberFormat`: axes get the short form by themselves) or the series `format`; `plugins.legend.display: false` → delete (`legend="auto"` shows it only with two or more series) or `legend={false}`; `plugins.legend.position` → `legend="top|bottom|right"`; `interaction: { intersect: false }` → delete; `plugins.zoom` → delete, or `zoom={false}` to turn zooming off; `plugins.tooltip.callbacks.label` returning `"label: value"` → the tooltip shows the series name by itself, so return only the value, or use `tooltipSnippet`. `indexAxis: 'y'` → `horizontal`; `scales.x.stacked` / `scales.y.stacked: true` → `stacked`; a dataset with `type: 'line'` and `yAxisID: 'share'` plus `scales.share` → `type: 'line', axis: 'right', format` on the series and no scale.

manual.summary: The trick of one dataset per bar (each with a single value and `stacked: true`) to get one color per bar is no longer needed.
manual.action: Use one series with all the values and an array in `color` (one color per bar); remove `stacked` if it was there only for the trick. The tooltip and the hidden table then show one row per category.

manual.summary: Horizontal charts grow with the rows by themselves (`--bar-chart-row-height`, 2.5rem = 40px): the wrappers sized `labels.length * 40px` are no longer needed.
manual.action: With `horizontal`, remove the `<div style="height: {labels.length * 40}px">` around the chart and its scroll container. To keep a fixed height with the rows scrolling inside, set `--bar-chart-height`.

manual.summary: v5 draws the charts like the design prototype: ticks on both axes (v4 hid them), legend below and only with two or more series (v4 always on top), HTML tooltip card, thicker rounded bars, dashed grid.
manual.action: Open the screen and compare: where the app relied on the hidden ticks (very small charts, sparklines), pass `options={{ scales: { x: { ticks: { display: false } }, y: { ticks: { display: false } } } }}`.

added: `horizontal`, `stacked`, `format`, `legend`, `zoom` (props for the common options).
`label` names the chart for screen readers, which also read a hidden table of the values.
`onitemclick({ index, datasetIndex, label, value, event })` on a bar.
`tooltipSnippet`, `legendSnippet`.
`locale`, `resetZoomLabel`.
`chart` (the chart.js instance) and `barChartElement` are bindable.
CSS variables `--bar-chart-*` for size, grid, ticks, bars, legend and tooltip.

toCssVar.name: gap
toCssVar.note: Default 12px instead of 15px.

types.name: boxes
types.v4: { name: string; label: string; href?: string; style?: { width?: string; maxWidth?: string; minWidth?: string } }[]
types.note: `style` is gone (see the `box-list-grid` step). New optional fields: `description`, `icon`, `color`, `disabled`, `class`, `data`.

changed.name: onboxClick
changed.note: Still called for links, before the navigation. Not called for disabled boxes.

parameters.name: boxSnippet
parameters.note: v4 replaced the whole box, so the snippet had to draw its own `<a>` or `<button>` (and lost `onboxClick`). v5 renders it inside the link or button of the library: drop the outer `<a>`/`<button>` from the snippet and keep only its content.

manual.summary: Boxes that navigate with `goto` inside `onboxClick` can be links.
manual.action: Where `onboxClick` only maps `box.name` to a URL and calls `goto`, put the URL in `href` on each box and remove the handler: the box becomes a real link (middle click, open in a new tab, preload by SvelteKit) and a wrong name can no longer leave a box doing nothing.

manual.summary: The boxes are a grid of cards as wide as the column (`--box-list-min-width`, 240px, as many columns as fit, one on a phone) instead of a row of pills as wide as their text.
manual.action: Drop `style.width`, `style.minWidth` and `style.maxWidth` from the boxes; for narrower or wider columns set `--box-list-min-width` on the list. Wrappers that limited the width of the list can usually stay.

manual.summary: New look: a card with border, optional icon tile, label 14px 600 and description under it; no arrow; focus ring instead of the blue background that stayed after a click.
manual.action: Usually nothing to do. To keep the v4 arrow add `appendSnippet` with `<Icon path={mdiArrowRight} />`. Remove app CSS that targeted `.box` or the v4 `:focus` colors; the parts are `.aurora-box-list-box`, `-icon`, `-label`, `-description`, styled with the `--box-list-*` variables.

manual.summary: Most apps use a local copy (`$lib/components/common/BoxList.svelte`) instead of the library one, often with `icon` and a `description` shown on hover.
manual.action: Replace the copy with the library `BoxList` and delete it: `icon` becomes an `@mdi/js` path, `description` is kept (always visible now; for HTML use `descriptionSnippet` with `{@html box.description}`), `redirectUrl` / `url` → `href` (SvelteKit preloads links by itself), drop `expanded`, `animateOnMount` and the `type` prop. `on:box-click={(e) => ...e.detail.box}` → `onboxClick={({ box }) => ...}`, or `href` as in `box-list-navigation`. A `prepend` slot that added a custom card has no equivalent: render that card next to the list (for example in a grid that holds both).

added: `description` per box, always visible, read as the description of the box by screen readers.
`icon` per box (an `@mdi/js` path in a tile) and `color` for its tone (`primary` or a data color 1–6).
`disabled` and `class` per box; `data` for app data passed back to the snippets.
`onclick` per box, called before `onboxClick`; it makes a box without `href` a button.
Boxes without `href` and without `onboxClick` render as plain cards (v4 drew a button that did nothing).

manual.summary: With `range` the same day clicked twice is a one-day range (`selectedDateTo` equals `selectedDate`; v4 ignored the second click), the third click starts a new range, and hovering or focusing a day previews the band.

manual.summary: It is an ARIA grid: one Tab stop, arrows move by day and week, Home and End to the ends of the week, Page Up and Page Down change month (with Shift, year), Enter and Space choose; screen readers read the full date of each day and the grid is named by the month. v4 cells were not focusable.
manual.action: End-to-end tests that clicked a `.day-slot` by its number should use `getByRole("gridcell", { name: <full date> })` (the name comes from `Intl` in `locale`). With a visible title next to the grid, point `aria-labelledby` at it.

manual.summary: Always 6 rows of 32px days (v4: only the rows needed, stretched to `--calendar-height`, 100% of the parent); short weekday names ("Mon", v4 one bold letter); today marked by a dot (v4: pale red circle); the selected day a primary fill; outside days at 50% opacity (v4: 30%); the range a continuous band; the new month slides in.

manual.action: Choose a `variant` by meaning: `primary` (tinted primary), `success` / `warning` / `error` for statuses, `accent`, or `filled` for the strong v4-like look (primary gradient, light text). Chips colored entirely by their own CSS variables keep them through the renames. Toggle chips get the filled look from `selected`.

manual.summary: On a toggle chip v4 `--chip-background-color`, `--chip-color` and `--chip-hover-background-color` styled only the active state; v5 `--chip-background`, `--chip-color` and `--chip-hover-background` apply in every state. manual.action: On chips with `inactive` (now `selected`), put the v4 active values in `--chip-selected-background`, `--chip-selected-color`, `--chip-selected-border-color`, and the v4 `--chip-inactive-*` values in `--chip-background`, `--chip-color`, `--chip-border-color`. v5 has one `--chip-hover-background` / `--chip-hover-color` for both states: where v4 set different hover colors for active and inactive chips, keep one, or drop both (the hover keeps the state colors and lifts the chip). manual.summary: The chip is an inline-flex `<span>` that holds a native `<button>` only with `onclick`, and the close button is a sibling of it; v4 was a block-level `<div role="button" class="chip">` (`display: flex`) with the close button inside, focusable only with `buttonTabIndex`.
manual.action: Chips in a block container no longer take the whole row: put them in a flex container, or set `display: flex` through `class` where they must stretch. A chip meant to be clickable needs `onclick` (it is focusable and has hover only then). Rewrite app CSS that targets `.chip`, `.chip.inactive`, `.text`, `.icon-after` or `[role="button"]` against `.aurora-chip`, `[data-selected]`, `.aurora-chip-text`, `.aurora-chip-close`.

manual.action: Use `size="sm"` in dense lists and tables; `--chip-height` and `--chip-font-size` for other sizes. Long text is cut with an ellipsis: pass `title` where the full text must be readable.

manual.summary: The close click is no longer stopped: it bubbles to the ancestors of the chip.
manual.action: If an ancestor handles clicks (a clickable row or card, a field that opens a menu), call `event.stopPropagation()` in `onclose`. The chip `onclick` is not affected: the close button sits outside the chip button.

manual.summary: Country names come from the browser (`Intl.DisplayNames`) in `locale` (default: the one of `setDefaultLocale`, else `en`) and the list is sorted by name in that language; v4 had fixed English ISO names sorted by code. In English 48 of the 249 names differ (for example "Czech Republic" → "Czechia").
manual.action: Italian apps call `setDefaultLocale("it")` in the root layout (step `global-default-locale`) or pass `locale="it"`; the texts of the field (chip remove buttons, empty list) follow the same locale. Store and compare the ISO code (`value`), never the label: code that matched hard-coded v4 names breaks.

manual.summary: The labels of `values` are always replaced by the name in `locale`, also in `onchange` and in the bound `values`.
manual.action: Remove code that built labels for the selected countries (`getCountryInfoByAlpha2(code).name`): `[{ value: code }]` is enough. A custom label on a value is not kept: use `chipLabelSnippet` to show other text.

manual.summary: Flags are 4:3 (v4: square) and are the icons of options and chips (`itemIconSnippet`, `chipIconSnippet`) instead of being drawn inside the label snippets.
manual.action: Size them with `--flag-icon-size` on the component. For square flags pass `itemIconSnippet` and `chipIconSnippet` that render `<FlagIcon alpha2={String(item.value)} square />`. A `chipLabelSnippet` or `itemLabelSnippet` passed through `autocompleteProps` was ignored in v4; passed directly it now replaces only the text, next to the flag.

manual.summary: The search ignores accents, also matches the ISO code ("us" → United States) and ranks the results: names that start with the text, then the code, then names with a word that starts with it, then the rest.
manual.action: Remove app workarounds that searched codes or stripped accents.

manual.summary: Values are compared with `===` (v4 mixed `==` and `===`) and duplicate `value`s in `items` or `values` throw.
manual.action: Check that `values` use the same type as `items` (`{ value: 1 }` and `{ value: "1" }` are different options now: ids read from the URL or a form are strings) and that `items` has no duplicate `value`.

manual.summary: It is an ARIA combobox: the focus stays in the input and options are not tab stops (neither is the v4 wrapper). While typing, the first match is highlighted and Enter picks it without submitting the form; Backspace on an empty field removes the last value; Escape closes the list and keeps the focus; the arrows do not move the caret.
manual.action: Check forms where Enter in the field was expected to submit while an option is highlighted, and end-to-end tests that tabbed into the options or clicked the wrapper; use `getByRole("combobox")` and `getByRole("option")`.

manual.summary: `closeOnSelect={true}` now also closes the list with `multiple` (v4 ignored it there).
manual.action: Remove `closeOnSelect` from `multiple` usages that must keep the list open.

manual.summary: `searchText` keeps its initial value (v4 erased it after mount) and becomes `""` (not `undefined`) when the list closes.
manual.action: Replace checks like `searchText === undefined` with `!searchText`.

manual.summary: With single selection, picking another option calls `onchange` with the replaced value in `unselect` as well as the new one in `select`.
manual.action: Check handlers that treat `unselect` as "the user cleared the field": test `select === undefined` (or `selection.length === 0`) instead.

manual.summary: `disabled` disables the native input: it gets no focus, the list does not open and chips have no remove button. With `mandatory` the last chip has no remove button either.
manual.action: Check flows that relied on focusing or opening a disabled Autocomplete (v4 only faded it).

manual.summary: With `mobileDrawer`, on screens up to 1024px the list opens in a bottom drawer that has its own search field and a title (`drawerTitle ?? label`); the field on the page becomes read-only. v4 showed only the list. The server renders the desktop variant.
manual.action: Pass `label` or `drawerTitle` so the drawer has a title; pass `drawerSearch={false}` for short lists that need no search.

manual.summary: `itemSnippet` replaces the content of an option, not the option: the row keeps its click handling, `role="option"`, the selected and highlighted states and their styles.
manual.action: Remove from the snippet the wrapper that drew the row (click handlers, padding, selected or focused backgrounds) and keep only the content; use `selected` and `highlighted` from the parameters for content that changes with the state.

manual.summary: `itemLabelSnippet` replaces only the label: the `item.icon` and the check mark of selected options stay (v4 dropped the icon).
manual.action: If the snippet drew the icon itself, remove it from the snippet or move it to `itemIconSnippet`.

manual.summary: `hintSnippet` renders inside the hint element (linked to the input with `aria-describedby`) instead of in place of it.
manual.action: Remove wrappers or margins the snippet added to position itself under the field.

manual.summary: New look: the field uses the `--global-input-*` base (36px minimum height, input border and focus ring), takes 100% of the container width, chips are primary `sm` Chips, the selected options are tinted with a check mark (v4: filled primary) and the list is as wide as the field, at most 300px high.
manual.action: Check layouts where an Autocomplete sat in a row next to other elements: set `--autocomplete-width` (a length or `auto`) or size its container. Drop `--chip-*` overrides that targeted the v4 chips if they now look wrong.

manual.summary: Internal classes changed: `.selection-container` → `.aurora-autocomplete-field`, `.autocomplete-input` → `.aurora-autocomplete-field input`, `.selection-item` → `.aurora-autocomplete-option`, `.focused` → `[data-highlighted]`, `.selected` → `[data-selected]`, `.not-visible-chip-number` → `.aurora-autocomplete-counter`, `.hint` → `.aurora-autocomplete-hint`, `li.item-N` → `[role="option"]`.
manual.action: Rewrite app `:global(...)` selectors that target them, or replace them with `--autocomplete-*` variables.

added: Every Autocomplete prop, snippet and callback directly on the component, and the `--autocomplete-*` variables.
`locale`, `dialCode` (dialing code at the end of each option), `class.dialCode`.
Utilities `countryCodes`, `countryName(code, locale)`, `dialCode(code)`, `countryItems(locale, codes?)` and the `CountryData` type.
`--countries-autocomplete-dial-code-color`, `-font-family`, `-font-size`.

renamed.note: Now a maximum, and optional: without it the dashboard grows downwards. Read-only, only the rows in use are shown (v4 always drew `layoutHeight` rows, empty ones included); while editing, a free band as tall as the tallest catalog size stays below the widgets. A `layoutHeight` computed from the rows in use (used rows + tallest widget) is no longer needed: drop it.

Each entry: `availableSizes: [height, width][]` → `sizes: { width, height }[]` (mind the order), `icon: "mdi-..."` → an SVG path from `@mdi/js`. New optional `category` and `unique`. Entries are shown in the given order (v4 sorted them by title with "Placeholder" first).
Same meaning: true when a row in use has an empty cell.
`editing` also turns on removing, moving and resizing. `canAdd={false}` → nothing (read-only is the default).

defaults.name: editing

changed.name: widgets

changed.name: preview

changed.note: Called for every change (add, remove, move, resize) with the widgets themselves (v4 passed an internal cell): check `added.length > 0` to react to additions only.

changed.note: Called for every change: check `removed.length > 0`. When both v4 callbacks are used, merge them in one `onchange`.

manual.summary: A DashboardShaper is read-only unless `editing` is set; while editing, widgets can also be moved and resized (v4: only added and removed).
manual.action: On the pages that create or edit a dashboard add `editing` (replacing `canAdd`, `canDelete` and similar app props). The layout is saved as before (`left`, `top`, `width`, `height`); to keep exactly the v4 behaviour pass `movable={false} resizable={false}`. Remove delete overlays drawn in `widgetCellSnippet`: the dashboard shows its own remove button while editing.

manual.summary: `availableWidgetCells` became `catalog`, with `sizes: { width, height }[]` instead of `availableSizes: [height, width][]` (the codemod converts the entries written in the same file), and a new `unique`.
manual.action: For widget types the backend keeps once per dashboard (saved by `name`) add `unique: true`. Catalogs filtered by permission stay as they are.

manual.summary: Apps with their own copy of DashboardShaper (with a DashboardEditor wrapper and `componentName`) can use the library one.
manual.action: Replace the local DashboardShaper/DashboardEditor/DashboardAddButton with the library DashboardShaper: map `componentName` to `name` when loading and back when saving (or keep `componentName` in `data`), move the catalog to `catalog`, the widget switch to `widgetSnippet`, and the data loading to `onchange` (`added`).

added: Moving widgets by dragging (mouse, or touch after a hold) and with the arrow keys; swapping two widgets of the same size.
Resizing among the `sizes` of the catalog with the corner handle or Shift and the arrow keys; `movable` and `resizable` to turn them off.
`stackBelow`, `catalogItemSnippet`, `labels`, `class` per part, `category` and `unique` in the catalog.
Announcements for screen readers and a keyboard handle on each widget while editing.
On narrow screens, editing on a small version of the grid: tap a block to select it, then drag it, resize it from its handle or remove it; holding any block drags it too.
On touch screens, holding a widget starts the drag, so swiping still scrolls the page.
`--dashboard-shaper-*` variables for slots, editing controls, drop target, catalog and min height.

renamed.note: A boolean now: see `props.values`. A dynamic `type={t}` → `range={t === "dateRange"}`.

removed.name: selectedYear
removed.note: v4 wrote the year chosen in the year view here, not linked to the date. Use `bind:visibleYear` (the year shown) or read the year of `selectedDate`. See `date-picker-navigation`.

removed.name: selectedMonth
removed.note: v4 wrote the month chosen in the month view here, not linked to the date. Use `bind:visibleMonth` (the month shown, 0 to 11) or read the month of `selectedDate`. See `date-picker-navigation`.

removed.name: selectableYears
removed.note: The years come from `min` and `max` (`Date`s, default years 1900–2100), which also disable the days, months and arrows outside them: `selectableYears={years}` → `min={new Date(first, 0, 1)} max={new Date(last, 11, 31)}`. Drop it when it only listed a wide span. A list with holes has no equivalent: use `isDateDisabled`. See `date-picker-years`.

removed.name: skipTabs
removed.note: Each view is a single Tab stop (the grid), and the title and arrows are buttons with accessible names. Drop it.

changed.name: view
changed.note: Now bindable (`bind:view`), and it follows the navigation: clicking the title goes day → month → year → day, choosing a year shows its months, choosing a month its days. v4 read it only at mount. Default `undefined`, which shows the days.

changed.name: disabled
changed.note: Disables everything: title, arrows and grids (v4: only clicks on days).

changed.name: class
changed.note: Still an object of classes per part, with other keys: `container` unchanged; `selectorRow` (the row with the arrows) → `header`; v4 `header` (the colored band) is gone; new `title` (the title button) and `calendar` (the Calendar grid).

changed.name: visibleMonth
changed.note: Still bindable. The default is the month of `selectedDate` (v4: `selectedMonth`, the current month), and it follows `selectedDate` when that moves to another month.

changed.name: visibleYear
changed.note: Still bindable. The default is the year of `selectedDate` (v4: `selectedYear`, the current year). The arrows are limited by `min` / `max` (v4: by `selectableYears`).

defaults.name: locale
defaults.note: Without `locale` and without `setDefaultLocale` the title, the month and day names and the arrow labels are English and the week starts on Sunday. Call `setDefaultLocale("it")` once in the root layout (step `global-default-locale`); add `locale="it"` only to usages rendered outside it, unless the app wants English.

defaults.name: weekdayFormat
defaults.note: v4 had no prop and showed one letter per day; v5 shows short names. Add it only where the one-letter look matters.

values.name: range
values.note: For values that came from `type`: `type="dateRange"` → `range`, `type="singleDate"` → drop the attribute.

types.name: locale
types.note: Any locale `Intl` knows; names and the first day of the week come from it.

changed.name: ondayClick
changed.type: { date: Date; outside: boolean; nativeEvent: MouseEvent | KeyboardEvent }
changed.note: `dateStat` became `date`, a `Date` at local midnight: `dateStat.dayOfMonth` → `date.getDate()`, `.month` → `date.getMonth()`, `.year` → `date.getFullYear()`, `new Date(s.year, s.month, s.dayOfMonth)` → `date`. v4 `dayOfWeek` was the column index (Monday = 0 with `it`, Sunday = 0 with `en`), not the weekday: `(date.getDay() + 6) % 7` for a Monday-first column, `date.getDay()` for the weekday. `selected` was always `!extraMonth`: use `!outside`. Called after the selection changed, only for days that can be chosen (never while `disabled`), also with Enter and Space. To follow the value, `onchange({ selectedDate, selectedDateTo })` or `bind:selectedDate` is simpler.

removed.name: onyearClick

removed.name: onmonthClick
removed.note: Choosing a month now shows its days without changing the date. Bind `visibleMonth` (and `view`) and react to them instead of `e.detail.month`. See `date-picker-navigation`.
