manual.summary: The panel is a title ("October 2026") between two arrows above the grid, on a popup surface 280px wide (border, radius, padding, shadow); the colored header with the year and the chosen date is gone and the height follows the content (v4: `100%` wide, 400px high).
manual.action: Drop `--date-picker-height` and the `--date-picker-header-*` variables. Set `--date-picker-width` where the v4 width mattered. Inside an app card that already draws a surface, set `--date-picker-border-width="0px"`, `--date-picker-box-shadow="none"` and `--date-picker-background="transparent"`.

manual.summary: Clicking the title goes from days to months to years and back; choosing a year shows its months and choosing a month its days, and neither changes the date. v4 had a year button in the header, wrote the choices to `selectedYear` / `selectedMonth` and reported them with `onyearClick` / `onmonthClick`.
manual.action: Replace `bind:selectedYear` / `bind:selectedMonth` and the `onyearClick` / `onmonthClick` handlers with `bind:visibleYear`, `bind:visibleMonth` and `bind:view`, read in a `$derived` or `$effect` where something must react.

manual.summary: The year view is a scrolling 4-column grid of every year from `min` to `max` (default 1900–2100), centered on the chosen one; v4 listed `selectableYears` (default the 75 years before and after the current one) and limited the arrows to them.
manual.action: Turn `selectableYears` into `min` / `max` dates (they also disable the days outside them), or drop it when it only listed a wide span.

manual.summary: The arrows have accessible names in the language of `locale` ("Previous month", "Mese precedente" in Italian; `previousMonthLabel`, `nextMonthLabel`, `previousYearLabel`, `nextYearLabel` change them) and all the buttons are `type="button"` (v4 header buttons submitted the forms they were in).
manual.action: Italian apps get the Italian names from `setDefaultLocale("it")` or `locale="it"`; pass the `*Label` props only for other names. Remove app code that prevented the header buttons from submitting a form.

manual.summary: `--calendar-*` variables set on a DatePicker still reach its grid. The renamed and removed ones are listed in `cssVars.removed`; the others keep their name with the meaning described in the Calendar rules.
manual.action: Apply the Calendar rules to them. `--calendar-selected-day-color` set to the text color on primary can be dropped; `--calendar-day-height` needs a length.

manual.summary: Markup and classes changed: `.date-picker-container`, `.header`, `.selector-row`, `.selector-text`, `button.year`, `button.day` → `.aurora-date-picker` (`data-view`, `data-disabled`), `.aurora-date-picker-header`, `.aurora-date-picker-title`; the grids are `.aurora-calendar`, `.aurora-month-selector`, `.aurora-year-selector`.
manual.action: Rewrite app `:global(...)` selectors that target the v4 classes, or replace them with `--date-picker-*` variables and `class.header` / `class.title`.

manual.summary: Days of the previous and next month can be chosen: a click selects the day and shows its month. v4 ignored the click (only `ondayClick` fired), and with `showExtraMonthDays={false}` the hidden cells still took clicks.
manual.action: Where outside days must stay inert, pass `showOutsideDays={false}` (the cells are empty) or limit the days with `min` / `max` / `isDateDisabled`. Handlers that tested `extraMonth` to ignore those clicks can drop the test.

manual.summary: With `range` the same day clicked twice is a one-day range (`selectedDateTo` equals `selectedDate`; v4 ignored the second click), the third click starts a new range, and hovering or focusing a day previews the band.
manual.action: Check code that treats `selectedDate` equal to `selectedDateTo` as impossible, or expected the second click on the start day to do nothing.

manual.summary: It is an ARIA grid: one Tab stop, arrows move by day and week, Home and End to the ends of the week, Page Up and Page Down change month (with Shift, year), Enter and Space choose; screen readers read the full date of each day and the grid is named by the month. v4 cells were not focusable.
manual.action: End-to-end tests that clicked a `.day-slot` by its number should use `getByRole("gridcell", { name: <full date> })` (the name comes from `Intl` in `locale`). With a visible title next to the grid, point `aria-labelledby` at it.

added: `min`, `max`, `isDateDisabled`, `weekStart`, `weekdayFormat`, `showOutsideDays`, `showWeekdays` (from Calendar).
`months={2}`: two months side by side in the day view, for long ranges; `--date-picker-month-width`, `--date-picker-months-gap`, `data-months`.
`titleSnippet`, `daySnippet`, `dayAppendSnippet`, `weekdaySnippet`, `footerSnippet` (content under the calendar, inside the panel).
`onchange({ selectedDate, selectedDateTo })`.
`previousMonthLabel`, `nextMonthLabel`, `previousYearLabel`, `nextYearLabel`.
`focus()` method, `bind:datePickerElement`, native attributes on the panel, `data-view` and `data-disabled`.
`--date-picker-*` variables for padding, gap, background, color, border and the title.

A boolean now: see `props.values`. A dynamic `type={t}` → `range={t === "dateRange"}`.

Only the tokens `dd`, `MM` and `yyyy`, with any separator (v4 accepted luxon tokens; hours were lost anyway). Without it the format now comes from `locale` (`it` dd/MM/yyyy, `en` MM/dd/yyyy): `pattern="dd/MM/yyyy"` can be dropped when the locale is `it` (`setDefaultLocale("it")` in the root layout or `locale="it"`).

defaults.name: locale
defaults.note: IMPORTANT. v4 had no `locale`: it was always Italian, dd/MM/yyyy, weeks from Monday. v5 takes the locale of the `locale` prop, else the one of `setDefaultLocale`, else English (MM/dd/yyyy, weeks from Sunday, English texts): with neither, a typed "05/03/2026" is read as May 3. Call `setDefaultLocale("it")` once in the root layout (step `global-default-locale`): then usages need no `locale="it"`, and the format, the calendar and the texts ("Inserisci una data valida", chip `gg/mm/aaaa`) are Italian. Add `locale="it"` only where the field renders outside that layout (an app wrapper used by other roots or by tests, a component mounted with `mount()`).

manual.summary: `ondayClick` is gone and the calendar closes by itself after a choice (with `range`, after the end). Most v4 usages had `bind:menuOpened={open}` plus `ondayClick={() => (open = false)}` only to close it: the codemod deletes those handlers.
manual.action: Delete `ondayClick` handlers that only close the menu, and `bind:menuOpened` / `bind:open` with its variable when nothing else reads it. Move any other code of the handler to `onchange({ selectedDate, selectedDateTo })` or to a `$derived` / `$effect` on the bound `selectedDate`.

manual.summary: Typing accepts digits only and adds the separators of `format`; paste (also `yyyy-MM-dd`) and autofill work, and the value updates on `input` (v4: on keydown after 30ms). A whole date that does not exist, is outside `min` / `max` or disabled, or an unfinished one when the field loses focus, shows the error state with `invalidText` ("Enter a valid date", in Italian "Inserisci una data valida") and makes the form invalid (`setCustomValidity`). Clicking a month or a year in the calendar no longer empties the text.
manual.action: With the Italian locale the message is already Italian; pass `invalidText` only for another message (`invalidText="Data non valida"`). Forms sent with `novalidate` or by script should still check `selectedDate`. Remove app code that validated or reformatted the typed text.

manual.summary: With `range` the field has a start and an end input separated by an arrow, named by `startLabel` / `endLabel` ("Start date" / "End date", in Italian "Data di inizio" / "Data di fine") after the `label`; a typed end before the start, or start after the end, is not accepted.
manual.action: Pass `startLabel` and `endLabel` only for other names than those of the locale. `placeholder` and `placeholderTo` keep their meaning.

manual.summary: Up to 1024px the calendar button opens the calendar in a bottom Drawer titled `drawerTitle ?? label` (v4: a centered Dialog); focusing the field does not open it and the field stays typable with the numeric keyboard. The server renders the desktop variant.
manual.action: Pass `label` or `drawerTitle` so the drawer has a title (`closeLabel` and `openLabel` follow the locale). `mobileDrawer={false}` keeps the menu on every screen.

manual.summary: The inputs are comboboxes: focus or click opens the calendar (desktop), Arrow Down moves the focus into it, Escape closes it and returns to the field, Tab closes it and moves on, Enter with the calendar open closes it without submitting the form.
manual.action: Check forms where Enter in an open date field was expected to submit, and end-to-end tests that clicked v4 calendar cells: use `getByRole("combobox")` and `getByRole("gridcell", { name: <full date> })`.

manual.summary: The field is 36px high with a border, the mono font, the calendar button at the start and a chip with the format at the end ("dd/mm/yyyy"), and it fills its container (v4: a 280px filled grey SimpleTextField in a `fit-content` wrapper). The calendar is a DatePicker in a Menu with the library surface (v4: 300px panel with the colored header).
manual.action: Set `--date-picker-text-field-width="280px"` where the v4 width mattered (fields in a row, toolbars, filters). `showFormat={false}` hides the chip when a `placeholder` already shows the format. Pass `label` instead of a separate label element when the app had one.

manual.summary: `--date-picker-*` and `--calendar-*` variables set on the field still reach the calendar, now also in the mobile drawer; the renamed and removed ones are listed in `cssVars.removed`. Apps often passed `--date-picker-header-color` with `--calendar-selected-day-color` set to `primary-foreground` for the v4 colored header.
manual.action: Drop the `--date-picker-header-*` variables and a `--calendar-selected-day-color` that only gave the text color on primary (the default). The shadow and border of the popup belong to the Menu (`--menu-box-shadow`, `--menu-border-radius`, ...), not to `--date-picker-box-shadow`. Apply the Calendar rules to the other `--calendar-*` names.

manual.summary: The inputs get generated ids (v4: fixed `from` and `to`, duplicated when a page had two fields).
manual.action: Replace `#from` / `#to` selectors, `getElementById("from")`, `<label for="from">` and test locators with the `id` prop (the start input; the end one is `<id>-to`), `label`, or `bind:input` / `bind:inputTo`.

manual.summary: Several apps wrap the field (`StandardDatePickerTextfield` in addibox, contattorapido, new-vigipass, stramoniumai); some wrappers forward only a few props (new-vigipass drops `menuOpened`, `ondayClick` and the rest).
manual.action: Migrate the wrapper first: type its props as `ComponentProps<typeof DatePickerTextField>` and spread `{...rest}` on the field, set `locale="it"` inside the wrapper when the app has no `setDefaultLocale("it")` (the Italian texts come with it: drop the Italian `invalidText`, `startLabel`, `endLabel`, `openLabel`, `closeLabel` the wrapper passed only to translate), and rename what it forwards (`menuOpened` → `open`, `type` → `range`, `oninput` → `onchange`). Then migrate its call sites with the same rules, since they pass the v4 names.

manual.summary: Markup and classes changed: `.date-picker-activator` and the SimpleTextField classes (`.textfield-container`, `.textfield`, `.row`, `.hint`) → `.aurora-date-picker-text-field` (`data-state`, `data-disabled`, `data-readonly`, `data-open`, `data-range`), `-label`, `-row`, `-control`, `-hint`; the calendar is `.aurora-date-picker` inside `.aurora-date-picker-text-field-menu` or the drawer.
manual.action: Rewrite app `:global(...)` selectors that target the v4 markup, or use the `class` parts and the `--date-picker-text-field-*` variables.

added: `label`, `labelSnippet`, `hint`, `hintSnippet`, `state`, `stateIconSnippet`, `invalidText`.
`min`, `max`, `isDateDisabled`, `weekStart`, `format`.
`name` / `nameTo`: hidden inputs that submit `yyyy-MM-dd`; `required`, `readonly`, `id`.
`clearable`, `clearLabel`, `clearSnippet`; `showFormat`, `formatLabel`, `formatSnippet`.
`months={2}`: two months side by side in the calendar menu (one in the mobile drawer).

`confirm`: the calendar works on a draft saved by an Apply button (Cancel, Escape and a click outside discard it; with `clearable` also a Clear button), as the local `DateRangePicker` copies did with `showApply` / `showClear`; `applyLabel`, `cancelLabel`.
`drawerTitle`, `closeLabel`, `openLabel`, `startLabel`, `endLabel`.

`locale` (BCP 47): language of the format, the calendar and the default texts, Italian with `it`, English otherwise; without it the one of `setDefaultLocale` (step `global-default-locale`), else `en`. Text props win over it.
`daySnippet`, `dayAppendSnippet`, `weekdayFormat`, `showOutsideDays` (forwarded to the calendar).
`bind:input`, `bind:inputTo`; native attributes and events of the (start) input.
`--date-picker-text-field-*` variables for the label, field, icons, format chip, separator, states and hint.

changed.name: title
changed.note: It also gives the initials of the avatar: first letter of the first and of the last word ("Mario Rossi" → "MR"); v4 took the first two letters ("MA"). `avatarText` still wins.

changed.name: onclick
changed.note: With `onclick` the component is a `<button>` (focus, Enter and Space, screen readers); v4 put the click on a `div role="presentation"`.

changed.name: --descriptive-avatar-cursor
changed.note: Defaults to `pointer` only with `onclick` or `href`, `auto` otherwise (v4: always `pointer`). Delete the overrides that set it to `auto`/`default`.

changed.name: --descriptive-avatar-image-gap
changed.note: Default 12px instead of 8px.

changed.name: --descriptive-avatar-title-font-size

manual.action: Delete `avatarText` where it only built initials from the same name; keep it for other text. Guard titles that may be missing ("undefined undefined").

manual.summary: The component is a real `<button>` with `onclick` (or a link with `href`); the apps wrapped it in clickable `div`s with `on:click`/`on:keypress`, sometimes with `aria-hidden`, and some called the handler twice.
manual.action: Remove the clickable wrappers and their `aria-hidden`, and pass the handler once as `onclick`; for navigation pass `href` instead of an `onclick` that calls `goto`. Remove `role="button"`/`tabindex` added by hand.

manual.summary: `children` replaces the title and subtitle even when neither is set (v4 ignored it without them); the avatar is no longer part of a `slot="avatar"`.
manual.action: Check the usages with `children`: the content now always shows. For a custom avatar use `avatarSnippet`.

manual.summary: `compact` shows only the avatar, with the title and subtitle in a Tooltip. App wrappers switched between DescriptiveAvatar and a bare Avatar (`showTitleAndDescription`) for collapsed sidebars.
manual.action: Replace the `{#if showTitleAndDescription}<DescriptiveAvatar …/>{:else}<Avatar …/>{/if}` switch with one `<DescriptiveAvatar … compact={!showTitleAndDescription} />`.

manual.summary: Clickable ones (`onclick`, `href`) have padding and a rounded hover background, as in the new design; the texts are smaller (14px / 12.5px) and the gap is 12px.
manual.action: Check the alignment where a clickable DescriptiveAvatar sits in a column with other content: set `--descriptive-avatar-padding="0"` to remove the padding. Restore the v4 sizes with the `--descriptive-avatar-*` variables where needed.

added: `href`, `target`, `rel`, `disabled`: link and disabled state.
`compact`: only the avatar, texts in a Tooltip.
All the `Avatar` props: `name`, `colorKey`, `color`, `size`, `shape`, `ring`, `status`, `icon`, `imageLoadingStatus`, `locale`, `badgeSnippet`.
`avatarSnippet`, `class`, native attributes and `descriptiveAvatarElement`.

`--descriptive-avatar-padding`, `--descriptive-avatar-border-radius`, `--descriptive-avatar-hover-background`, `--descriptive-avatar-title-color`, `--descriptive-avatar-subtitle-color`, `--descriptive-avatar-title-font-weight`.

removed.name: transition
removed.note: The entrance is set with CSS variables on the surface; exit plays the same movement backwards. `'fly-up'` (v4 default): `--dialog-transition-y="20px" --dialog-transition-scale="1"`; `'fly-down'`: `--dialog-transition-y="-20px" --dialog-transition-scale="1"`; `'scale'`: `--dialog-transition-y="0px" --dialog-transition-scale="0.7"`; `'fade'`: `--dialog-transition-y="0px" --dialog-transition-scale="1"`; `'fly-horizontal'`: `--dialog-transition-x="-20px" --dialog-transition-y="0px" --dialog-transition-scale="1"` (it now leaves from the side it came from). Without the prop the v5 default is a 16px rise with a 0.96 scale, close to `'fly-up'`.

removed.name: _overlayOpacity
removed.note: Fold the opacity into the backdrop color: `_overlayColor="#282828" _overlayOpacity="30%"` → `--dialog-backdrop-background="rgb(40 40 40 / 30%)"` (or `color-mix(in oklab, <color> 30%, transparent)`).

toCssVar.note: The variable takes the final translucent color: combine it with `_overlayOpacity` (v4 default 30%). v4 default look: `rgb(40 40 40 / 30%)`; the v5 default is `--global-color-overlay`.

toCssVar.name: _overlayBackdropFilter
toCssVar.note: The v5 default blurs 8px: pass `none` where the v4 dialog had no filter and the blur is unwanted.

toCssVar.name: _transitionTimingFunction
toCssVar.note: Used by both the entrance and the exit.

toCssVar.name: _transitionDuration
toCssVar.note: A CSS time (`0.5s`, `500ms`). v4 default 0.5s, v5 default 0.4s (`--global-duration-slow`).

renamed.note: v4 overwrote it inline from `_transitionDuration`; the app value now applies.
v4 overwrote it inline from `_transitionTimingFunction`; the app value now applies.

removed.note: Put the opacity in the backdrop color.

removed.name: --dialog-z-index
removed.note: The dialog is on the top layer and needs no z-index: remove the variable and any z-index logic around dialogs.

manual.summary: `children` sits inside a styled surface (background, border, radius, shadow, 20px padding, max width 440px) over a blurred backdrop; v4 rendered it bare, centered on a flat overlay.
manual.action: Where the app drew its own card in `children`, remove the card styles or pass `--dialog-padding="0" --dialog-background="transparent" --dialog-border-width="0" --dialog-box-shadow="none" --dialog-width="auto" --dialog-max-width="none"`. Content wider than 440px needs `--dialog-max-width`. App headers with a title and a close button can become `title` and `closable`, app footers `actionsSnippet`.

manual.summary: `persistent` now also blocks Escape; v4 closed every open dialog on Escape, persistent or not.
manual.action: Make sure every persistent dialog has a visible way to close: `closable`, a button that sets `open = false` or calls `close` from a snippet, or a `<form method="dialog">`.

manual.summary: The content mounts at every opening and unmounts after closing; v4 mounted it once and kept it, hidden, in the DOM.
manual.action: In the content, look for `onMount` / `$effect` that load data or register listeners (they now run at every opening), `bind:this` refs read while the dialog is closed (now `undefined`), and form values that must survive closing (move them to the parent). App tests that queried the hidden content must open the dialog first.

manual.summary: The dialog is a real `<dialog>` with `role="dialog"` and focus management; it needs an accessible name (v4 had no ARIA).
manual.action: Pass `title` (shown in the header and used as the name) or `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby` when the content has its own heading.

manual.summary: When the dialog opens, the first focusable element (or the one with `autofocus`) gets the focus, and the focus goes back to the opener on close.
manual.action: Remove app code that focused the first field after opening (often with `setTimeout`).

manual.summary: `topRightSnippet` sits 16px from the top right corner and `centerLeftSnippet` / `centerRightSnippet` are centered vertically 16px from the screen edges (`--dialog-inset`); v4 put the top right content at the very corner.
manual.action: Remove app margins or positioning that compensated the v4 placement, or set `--dialog-inset`. Each snippet receives `{ close }`: a close button in it can call `close` (which also calls `onclose`).

added: `title` / `titleSnippet` (also the accessible name), `closable` with `closeLabel` / `closeSnippet`, `actionsSnippet` as footer.
`locale` (BCP 47): language of the default texts, Italian with `it`, English otherwise; without it the one of `setDefaultLocale` (step `global-default-locale`), else `en`. Text props win over it.
`onclose(event)` when the dialog closes itself (Escape, backdrop, close button, `close`, `<form method="dialog">`).
Every snippet receives `{ close }`.
A `<form method="dialog">` inside closes it after a valid submit.
`bind:dialogElement`, `class` object (`dialog`, `backdrop`, `surface`, `header`, `title`, `body`, `actions`), native attributes on the `<dialog>`, `data-closing` while closing.
About 37 `--dialog-*` variables (surface, header, title, body, actions, backdrop, transition).

manual.summary: The divider is a native `<hr>` (a separator for screen readers) with class `aurora-divider`; v4 was an empty `<div>` styled inline.
manual.action: App CSS that targeted the v4 `div` (for example `.parent > div`) must target `.aurora-divider` or pass `class`. In a flex row a horizontal divider has no width of its own: give it `flex: 1` through `class`, or use `orientation="vertical"` if it separates items of the row.

manual.summary: The 5px left and right margins of v4 are gone: the line now spans the whole container.
manual.action: Usually nothing to do. Where the inset mattered, set `--divider-margin-left="5px"` and `--divider-margin-right="5px"` on that divider.

manual.summary: Most apps import their own `$lib/components/common/Divider.svelte` (props `color`, `weight`, `radius`, `marginTop`, `marginBottom`, `marginLeft`, `marginRight`), not the library one.
manual.action: Those copies are app code and keep working. To switch a usage to the library, import `Divider` from `@likable-hair/svelte` and turn the props into CSS variables: `color` → `--divider-color`, `weight` → `--divider-weight`, `radius` → `--divider-radius`, `marginTop` → `--divider-margin-top` (same for the other sides); the copy defaults to 5px on the sides like v4, the library to 0. Delete the copy when nothing imports it.

`label` and `children`: text in the middle of the line, read by screen readers.
`bind:dividerElement`, `class` and native attributes on the root.
`data-variant` and `data-orientation` attributes.
`--divider-spacing`, `--divider-vertical-min-height`, `--divider-gap` and `--divider-label-*` (color, font family, size, weight, letter spacing, text transform).

manual.summary: `labelSnippet` changed meaning: v4 replaced the whole button content, v5 `labelSnippet({ label })` renders only the prefix label before the selection.
manual.action: Move the v4 snippet to `valueSnippet({ values, text, placeholder })` for the selection text (`generatedLabel` → `text`), `iconSnippet({ icon })` for the icon, `chevronSnippet({ open })` for the arrow and `clearSnippet` for the clear icon. `handleCloseClick` is gone: the clear button is built in with `clearable`, or clear with `values = []`. `items`, `searchText` and `clearable` are no longer parameters: read them from the app state.

manual.summary: With more than one value the button reads "N selected", or "N selezionati" with the `it` locale (v4: always the Italian "N Selezionati", with a capital S, also with `lang="en"`).
manual.action: Italian apps get it from `setDefaultLocale("it")` or `locale="it"`. For another text pass `selectionText={(values) => ...}`.

manual.summary: The trigger is a `Button` (`variant="secondary"`, `size="md"`, 34px high) with the combobox role; v4 used a grey translucent button 38.78px high. Clicking it opens and closes the list, Enter, Space and the arrows open and pick, a letter jumps to the first option that starts with it, and Backspace never removes values.
manual.action: Check toolbars and filter rows: use `variant`, `size` and `--button-*` on the Dropdown for the v4 look. Remove app workarounds that closed the list on a second click. End-to-end tests find it with `getByRole("combobox", { name: label })`.

manual.summary: The clear X is a separate `<button>` ("Clear selection", `clearLabel`) next to the trigger, shown in place of the arrow while something is selected; clicking it does not open the list and gives the focus back to the trigger.
manual.action: Rewrite app CSS that targeted the X inside the v4 button; restyle it with `--dropdown-clear-*` or replace the icon with `clearSnippet`.

manual.summary: `disabled` disables the native button and hides the clear button; in v4 the list still opened and the X still cleared.
manual.action: Check flows that relied on clearing or opening a disabled Dropdown.

manual.summary: With `mobileDrawer`, on screens up to 1024px the list opens in a bottom drawer without a search field, titled with `label`, with the list focused. The server renders the desktop variant.
manual.action: Pass `label` so the drawer has a title.

manual.summary: `itemLabelSnippet` replaces only the label of an option: the `item.icon` and the check mark of selected options stay (v4 dropped the icon).
manual.action: If the snippet drew the icon itself, remove it from the snippet; `itemSnippet` replaces the whole content of the option.

manual.summary: `Item.icon` of the options is an SVG path (v4: an MDI class name).
manual.action: Apply the global icon transform to every `icon` in the `items` and `values` data (`"mdi-sort"` → `mdiSort` from `@mdi/js`).

manual.summary: Values are compared with `===` (v4 mixed `==` and `===`) and duplicate `value`s in `items` or `values` throw.
manual.action: Check that `values` use the same type as `items` (`1` and `"1"` are different options now) and that `items` has no duplicate `value`.

added: `label`: a prefix inside the button ("Sort by: Newest") and the accessible name.
`name` (a hidden input per selected value), `closeOnSelect`.
`variant` (default `secondary`) and `size` (default `md`) of the Button.
`selectionText(values)`, `clearLabel`, `closeLabel`, `noResultsText`.
`bind:buttonElement`, native `<button>` attributes and events, `class` object (`container`, `button`, `label`, `value`, `clear`, `menu`, `option`).
Snippets `iconSnippet`, `valueSnippet`, `chevronSnippet`, `clearSnippet`, `itemSnippet`, `emptySnippet`; callback `onclose`.
`--dropdown-*` variables (width, label, placeholder, chevron, clear button, menu minimum width); `--button-*` variables now reach the trigger.
`data-open`, `data-disabled` on the root and `data-empty` on the trigger.

unwrap.note: rows are the items themselves (`rows={items}`); where `subItems` were used, write `expandedSnippet({ row })` with a nested `Table`

renamed.note: Each header becomes a column with another shape: see `table-columns`.
`it` and `en` keep working; `locale` also sets the formatting of numbers and dates. Without it the table follows `setDefaultLocale`.
Number of rows of the whole result; the table computes the pages from it and `pageSize`.
Same `ilike` OR group in the query; setting it also shows the search field.

Same objects, drawn by the table as in v4 (the extra ones in a "More actions" menu): `label`, `icon`, `disabled`, `loading`, `info`, `disabledInfo` stay; `onClick(e)` → `onclick({ selected, selectedAll, excluded, count, clear, event })` (`e.detail.nativeEvent` → `event`), and a returned promise shows a spinner; `variant: 'danger'` is new. See `data-table-selection`.
Also accepts a function `(row) => key`.
The v4 `Filter[]` becomes `FilterField[]` (see the Filters rule): the conditions are no longer inside the definitions but in `bind:filterValue`. See `data-table-filters`.
Rows left out of `selectedAll`.
A "Columns" button in the toolbar instead of the "+" in the last header.

keys.note: The column manager cannot hide it, as in v4.

nested.note: `string` is the default text column; `number` is now formatted and right-aligned; `date` shows day, month and year in digits in the language of `locale` (`dateFormat` for Intl options), `datetime` also the time; `icon` and `checkbox` are gone (draw them with a `cell` snippet)

items.note: each header becomes a column: `value` → `key`, `type: { key, params }` → a flat `type` (`string` → none, `number`, `date` or `datetime`, `boolean`, `custom`), `params.nullText` → `empty`, `locked` → `required`, `sortModify` → `sort` with `{ builder, direction }`; `icon` and `checkbox` columns are gone (use a `cell` snippet), `data` is gone

manual.summary: `headers` become `columns`: `value` → `key`, `type: { key, params }` → a flat `type` and options. `string` → `text` (or no type), `number` → `number` (now formatted and right-aligned), `date` with a luxon `format` → `date` or `datetime` with `dateFormat` (Intl options, language from `locale`), `custom` stays `custom`, `icon` and `checkbox` are gone (they ignored the value). `nullText` → `empty` (also when it was a function: use `format` or `cell`), `sortModify` → `sort` with `{ builder, direction }` instead of `{ builder, sortDirection }`, `minWidth`/`maxWidth`/`width` accept any CSS length, `pinned` stays, `locked` and `data` are gone.
manual.action: Rewrite each header object. A `date` column with `{ format: 'dd/MM/yyyy', locale: 'it' }` usually needs no options: the default is day, month and year in digits in the language of `locale`; luxon values still work. Remove `icon` columns or draw the icon with a `cell` snippet. Where a header had `width` in %, keep it: it is a preferred width; use `minWidth` when the column must not shrink.

manual.summary: `customSnippet` (now `cellSnippet`) usually holds a chain `{#if header.value == 'a'} … {:else if header.value == 'b'} …`. It keeps working with `column.key`, but every column can carry its own `cell` snippet, and formatting that v4 apps did by hand is now built in: dates (`type: 'date'`), money (`type: 'number', numberFormat: { style: 'currency', currency: 'EUR' }`), yes/no (`type: 'boolean'`), empty text (`empty`).
manual.action: The codemod renames the parameters (`header` → `column`, `item` → `row`, `header.value` → `.key`). Then, branch by branch, replace hand-made formatting with the column type, and move the remaining branches to top-level snippets referenced by `cell` in the column definition; delete `cellSnippet` when it is empty.

manual.summary: About half of the row click handlers only navigate (`goto('/x/' + item.id)`). `rowHref` makes the row a real link: Ctrl-click and middle click open a new tab, SvelteKit preloads it, keyboard and screen readers reach it.
manual.action: Where `onrowClick` only calls `goto(url)`, replace it with `rowHref={(row) => url}`. Keep `onrowclick` for actions that are not a page (opening a dialog, selecting).

manual.summary: Above 200 rows (`virtualize`) only the rows in view, plus a margin, are in the page; the others are drawn while scrolling and the columns keep the widths of the first rows. The find of the browser (Ctrl+F) and printing see only the drawn rows.
manual.action: Usually nothing to do. Where a page must show every row in the DOM (printing, Ctrl+F on long lists, tests or scripts that query all the rows), pass `virtualize={false}`, or a higher threshold such as `virtualize={1000}`.

manual.summary: v4 split one query in three callbacks (`onpaginationChange`, `onfiltersChange`, `onsort`) whose bodies were almost the same (load the page with `{ page, perPage, filtersBuilder }`), never reset the page and dropped the search from the builder of a page change. v5 has one `onquerychange(query)` with `{ page, pageSize, sort, search, filterValue, builder }`, the page already back to 1 after a change of filters, search, sorting or page size.
manual.action: Replace the handlers with one `onquerychange={(query) => load(query)}` that calls the service with `query.page`, `query.pageSize` and `query.builder`, then sets `rows`, `total` and `loading`; delete `page = 1` resets and the `filtersBuilder` kept in the page. Better, replace the whole thing with a `loader` (see `data-table-loader`).

manual.summary: With `loader={(query) => service.list(...)}` returning `{ rows, total }` the table loads by itself: loading state, aborted outdated requests, error with "Retry", page past the end, `reload()` after a create or delete. The first page from the `load` of SvelteKit goes in `rows` and `total`, so it is not loaded twice.
manual.action: Write `loader={async ({ page, pageSize, builder, signal }) => { const res = await service.list({ page, perPage: pageSize, filtersBuilder: builder }, { signal }); return { rows: res.data, total: res.meta.total }; }}` (or `pageCount: res.meta.lastPage`), pass `rows={data.rows}` and `total={data.total}` from `load`, and delete the handlers, `loading` and `maxPage` state. Call `table.reload()` (with `bind:this={table}`) where the page reloaded the list after saving.

manual.summary: `filters` (v4 `Filter[]`, definition and value together) becomes `filterFields` (`FilterField[]`, definitions only) plus `bind:filterValue` (the tree of conditions, as the `value` of Filters).
manual.action: Convert each `Filter` to a `FilterField` as the Filters rule says (`filters-fields`); where the page read the active values from `filters`, read `filterValue` (or `query.filterValue`) instead. Initial conditions go in `filterValue={createFilters([filterCondition(...)])}`.

manual.summary: The quick filters of the v4 tables (two incompatible models in PaginatedTable and DynamicTable) are fields of the Filters: `pinned` keeps a field as a pill in the bar, `presets` are chips with ready conditions. A "missing value" is the operator `empty`; a boolean with three states is `isTrue` / `isFalse` / no condition.
manual.action: For each quick filter add `pinned: true` to its field in `filterFields`; for ready-made choices pass `filtersProps={{ presets: [{ id, label, conditions }] }}`. Move the `modify` of custom quick filters to the `apply` of the field.

manual.summary: The selection keeps working across pages and has one model: `bind:selected`, plus `selectedAll` and `excluded` once the user picks "Select all N" in the bar (v4 PaginatedTable could not exclude rows and cleared `selectedItems` at every page). It is cleared when filters or search change. The header checkbox selects the rows of the page (v4 PaginatedTable: every row). The v4 `Action` objects keep working as `selectionActions`.
manual.action: Rename `actionsForSelectedItems` to `selectionActions` and, in each `onClick`, read the selection from the argument (`onclick: ({ selected, selectedAll, excluded, event }) => ...`) instead of the bound `selectedItems`; when `selectedAll` is true send the query (`builder`) and `excluded` to the backend instead of the ids. Destructive actions can take `variant: 'danger'`. Where the bar must not show, pass `selectionBar={false}`.

manual.summary: Apps saved the visible headers as `[{ name, order }]` in the user settings (`populateHeaders`, 53 times). v5 keeps the order, visibility, widths and pins as `columnState` = `[{ key, visible, width?, pinned? }]`, plain data.
manual.action: Keep the setting key and store `columnState` instead: restore it with `columnState={settings.value}` (old values: map `[{ name, order }]` to `{ key: name, visible: true }` in order, the others hidden) and save it in `oncolumnstatechange({ columnState })`, called when the user saves the view or resizes a column. Delete `populateHeaders` and the hand-made column drawers.

manual.summary: Many apps wrap the v4 tables (`StandardPaginatedTable`, `<Entity>PaginatedTable`, a `PaginatedTable` with `fetcher` in evote and epass, `LocalPaginatedTable` in lupette) mostly to repeat the same fetch, the same defaults (`lang="it"`, `editFilterMode`) and the same column drawer.
manual.action: Migrate the wrapper once to `DataTable` with a `loader`, then check whether it still adds anything: set `setDefaultLocale('it')` in the root layout instead of `lang`, and use `columnManager` instead of the copied drawer. For rows already in memory (LocalPaginatedTable) use `Table` with `Paginator`: DataTable always asks the server.

manual.summary: Default look of the prototype: one bordered box with the toolbar on top (search, filter pills, "Columns", the app buttons on the right), the table and a footer with "Rows per page", "1–20 of 312" and the paginator; the selection bar floats at the bottom of the table. Below the `cardBreakpoint` of the table the frame goes away and the rows become cards.
manual.action: Usually accept it. Remove page CSS that drew a box or a toolbar around the v4 table. App CSS on `.paginated-table`, `.searchbar-and-filter-container` or `.footer` must target `.aurora-data-table`, `.aurora-data-table-toolbar`, `.aurora-data-table-footer` or use the `class` parts.

manual.summary: DynamicTable wanted `rows: { item, subItems }[]` (62 mappings in the apps) and drew the sub-rows with `subHeaders` and the `subRow*` snippets. v5 takes plain rows; the detail of a row is `expandedSnippet`, where a sub-table is a nested `Table`.
manual.action: Pass the items directly (`rows={items}` instead of `items.map((item) => ({ item, subItems: [] }))`), read `row` instead of `row.item` in the snippets. Where `subItems` were used, write `expandedSnippet({ row })` with `<Table rows={row.lines} columns={subColumns} />`.

manual.summary: The inline cell editor (`cellEdit`, `cellEditorInfo`, `onsaveCellEdit`) is gone: it was active in two apps only and edited the wrong row after scrolling.
manual.action: In the `cell` snippet of an editable column put a small field that saves on change, or a button that opens a Dialog with the form; save there and call `reload()` or update the row in `rows`.

added: `loader({ ...query, signal })` with `onloaded`, `onerror`, `errorSnippet` and `reload()`.
`pagination`: `pages`, `infinite` (with `onloadmore` when there is no `loader`) or `none`.
`search` bindable, `searchable`, `filterValue` bindable, `filtersProps`, `searchBarProps`, `paginatorProps`, `columnManagerProps`.
`columnManager`: "Columns" button with the `ColumnManager`; `oncolumnstatechange` on save and resize.
Selection bar with "Select all N", `selectionActions` (with `variant: 'danger'` and promises that spin), `selectionDisabled`, `selectionActionsSnippet` for extra content, `selectionBar`, `excluded`.
`pageSizes`, `pageCount`, `rangeSnippet`, `searchSnippet`, `toolbarSnippet`, `labels`, `class` parts (`container`, `toolbar`, `footer`, `selectionBar`, `table`, `header`, `row`, `cell`).
`--data-table-*` variables for the frame, the toolbar, the footer, the messages and the selection bar.
Every prop of `Table`: `expandedSnippet`, `rowHref`, `actionsSnippet`, `actionsVisibility`, cards, `columnState`, `columnsKey`.

renamed.note: Each header becomes a column with another shape: see `table-columns`.
Same function `(row) => classes`; it may now also return an array or an object, like `class`.
`it` and `en` keep working; `locale` also sets the formatting of numbers and dates. Without it the table follows `setDefaultLocale`.
Number of rows of the whole result; the table computes the pages from it and `pageSize`.
Same `ilike` OR group in the query; setting it also shows the search field.

Same objects, drawn by the table as in v4 (the extra ones in a "More actions" menu): `label`, `icon`, `disabled`, `loading`, `info`, `disabledInfo` stay; `onClick(e)` → `onclick({ selected, selectedAll, excluded, count, clear, event })` (`e.detail.nativeEvent` → `event`), and a returned promise shows a spinner; `variant: 'danger'` is new. See `data-table-selection`.
Also accepts a function `(row) => key`.
The v4 `Filter[]` becomes `FilterField[]` (see the Filters rule): the conditions are no longer inside the definitions but in `bind:filterValue`. See `data-table-filters`.
Still bindable, default 20.
Pass `total` instead when it is known: the table computes the pages.

keys.note: The column manager cannot hide it, as in v4.

nested.note: `string` is the default text column; `number` is now formatted and right-aligned; `date` shows day, month and year in digits in the language of `locale` (`dateFormat` for Intl options), `datetime` also the time; `icon` and `checkbox` are gone (draw them with a `cell` snippet)

items.note: each header becomes a column: `value` → `key`, `type: { key, params }` → a flat `type` (`string` → none, `number`, `date` or `datetime`, `boolean`, `custom`), `params.nullText` → `empty`, `locked` → `required`, `sortModify` → `sort` with `{ builder, direction }`; `icon` and `checkbox` columns are gone (use a `cell` snippet), `data` is gone

manual.summary: `headers` become `columns`: `value` → `key`, `type: { key, params }` → a flat `type` and options. `string` → `text` (or no type), `number` → `number` (now formatted and right-aligned), `date` with a luxon `format` → `date` or `datetime` with `dateFormat` (Intl options, language from `locale`), `custom` stays `custom`, `icon` and `checkbox` are gone (they ignored the value). `nullText` → `empty` (also when it was a function: use `format` or `cell`), `sortModify` → `sort` with `{ builder, direction }` instead of `{ builder, sortDirection }`, `minWidth`/`maxWidth`/`width` accept any CSS length, `pinned` stays, `locked` and `data` are gone.
manual.action: Rewrite each header object. A `date` column with `{ format: 'dd/MM/yyyy', locale: 'it' }` usually needs no options: the default is day, month and year in digits in the language of `locale`; luxon values still work. Remove `icon` columns or draw the icon with a `cell` snippet. Where a header had `width` in %, keep it: it is a preferred width; use `minWidth` when the column must not shrink.

manual.summary: `customSnippet` (now `cellSnippet`) usually holds a chain `{#if header.value == 'a'} … {:else if header.value == 'b'} …`. It keeps working with `column.key`, but every column can carry its own `cell` snippet, and formatting that v4 apps did by hand is now built in: dates (`type: 'date'`), money (`type: 'number', numberFormat: { style: 'currency', currency: 'EUR' }`), yes/no (`type: 'boolean'`), empty text (`empty`).
manual.action: The codemod renames the parameters (`header` → `column`, `item` → `row`, `header.value` → `.key`). Then, branch by branch, replace hand-made formatting with the column type, and move the remaining branches to top-level snippets referenced by `cell` in the column definition; delete `cellSnippet` when it is empty.

manual.summary: About half of the row click handlers only navigate (`goto('/x/' + item.id)`). `rowHref` makes the row a real link: Ctrl-click and middle click open a new tab, SvelteKit preloads it, keyboard and screen readers reach it.
manual.action: Where `onrowClick` only calls `goto(url)`, replace it with `rowHref={(row) => url}`. Keep `onrowclick` for actions that are not a page (opening a dialog, selecting).

manual.summary: Above 200 rows (`virtualize`) only the rows in view, plus a margin, are in the page; the others are drawn while scrolling and the columns keep the widths of the first rows. The find of the browser (Ctrl+F) and printing see only the drawn rows.
manual.action: Usually nothing to do. Where a page must show every row in the DOM (printing, Ctrl+F on long lists, tests or scripts that query all the rows), pass `virtualize={false}`, or a higher threshold such as `virtualize={1000}`.

manual.summary: v4 split one query in three callbacks (`onpaginationChange`, `onfiltersChange`, `onsort`) whose bodies were almost the same (load the page with `{ page, perPage, filtersBuilder }`), never reset the page and dropped the search from the builder of a page change. v5 has one `onquerychange(query)` with `{ page, pageSize, sort, search, filterValue, builder }`, the page already back to 1 after a change of filters, search, sorting or page size.
manual.action: Replace the handlers with one `onquerychange={(query) => load(query)}` that calls the service with `query.page`, `query.pageSize` and `query.builder`, then sets `rows`, `total` and `loading`; delete `page = 1` resets and the `filtersBuilder` kept in the page. Better, replace the whole thing with a `loader` (see `data-table-loader`).

manual.summary: With `loader={(query) => service.list(...)}` returning `{ rows, total }` the table loads by itself: loading state, aborted outdated requests, error with "Retry", page past the end, `reload()` after a create or delete. The first page from the `load` of SvelteKit goes in `rows` and `total`, so it is not loaded twice.
manual.action: Write `loader={async ({ page, pageSize, builder, signal }) => { const res = await service.list({ page, perPage: pageSize, filtersBuilder: builder }, { signal }); return { rows: res.data, total: res.meta.total }; }}` (or `pageCount: res.meta.lastPage`), pass `rows={data.rows}` and `total={data.total}` from `load`, and delete the handlers, `loading` and `maxPage` state. Call `table.reload()` (with `bind:this={table}`) where the page reloaded the list after saving.

manual.summary: `filters` (v4 `Filter[]`, definition and value together) becomes `filterFields` (`FilterField[]`, definitions only) plus `bind:filterValue` (the tree of conditions, as the `value` of Filters).
manual.action: Convert each `Filter` to a `FilterField` as the Filters rule says (`filters-fields`); where the page read the active values from `filters`, read `filterValue` (or `query.filterValue`) instead. Initial conditions go in `filterValue={createFilters([filterCondition(...)])}`.

manual.summary: The quick filters of the v4 tables (two incompatible models in PaginatedTable and DynamicTable) are fields of the Filters: `pinned` keeps a field as a pill in the bar, `presets` are chips with ready conditions. A "missing value" is the operator `empty`; a boolean with three states is `isTrue` / `isFalse` / no condition.
manual.action: For each quick filter add `pinned: true` to its field in `filterFields`; for ready-made choices pass `filtersProps={{ presets: [{ id, label, conditions }] }}`. Move the `modify` of custom quick filters to the `apply` of the field.

manual.summary: The selection keeps working across pages and has one model: `bind:selected`, plus `selectedAll` and `excluded` once the user picks "Select all N" in the bar (v4 PaginatedTable could not exclude rows and cleared `selectedItems` at every page). It is cleared when filters or search change. The header checkbox selects the rows of the page (v4 PaginatedTable: every row). The v4 `Action` objects keep working as `selectionActions`.
manual.action: Rename `actionsForSelectedItems` to `selectionActions` and, in each `onClick`, read the selection from the argument (`onclick: ({ selected, selectedAll, excluded, event }) => ...`) instead of the bound `selectedItems`; when `selectedAll` is true send the query (`builder`) and `excluded` to the backend instead of the ids. Destructive actions can take `variant: 'danger'`. Where the bar must not show, pass `selectionBar={false}`.

manual.summary: Apps saved the visible headers as `[{ name, order }]` in the user settings (`populateHeaders`, 53 times). v5 keeps the order, visibility, widths and pins as `columnState` = `[{ key, visible, width?, pinned? }]`, plain data.
manual.action: Keep the setting key and store `columnState` instead: restore it with `columnState={settings.value}` (old values: map `[{ name, order }]` to `{ key: name, visible: true }` in order, the others hidden) and save it in `oncolumnstatechange({ columnState })`, called when the user saves the view or resizes a column. Delete `populateHeaders` and the hand-made column drawers.

manual.summary: Many apps wrap the v4 tables (`StandardPaginatedTable`, `<Entity>PaginatedTable`, a `PaginatedTable` with `fetcher` in evote and epass, `LocalPaginatedTable` in lupette) mostly to repeat the same fetch, the same defaults (`lang="it"`, `editFilterMode`) and the same column drawer.
manual.action: Migrate the wrapper once to `DataTable` with a `loader`, then check whether it still adds anything: set `setDefaultLocale('it')` in the root layout instead of `lang`, and use `columnManager` instead of the copied drawer. For rows already in memory (LocalPaginatedTable) use `Table` with `Paginator`: DataTable always asks the server.

manual.summary: Default look of the prototype: one bordered box with the toolbar on top (search, filter pills, "Columns", the app buttons on the right), the table and a footer with "Rows per page", "1–20 of 312" and the paginator; the selection bar floats at the bottom of the table. Below the `cardBreakpoint` of the table the frame goes away and the rows become cards.
manual.action: Usually accept it. Remove page CSS that drew a box or a toolbar around the v4 table. App CSS on `.paginated-table`, `.searchbar-and-filter-container` or `.footer` must target `.aurora-data-table`, `.aurora-data-table-toolbar`, `.aurora-data-table-footer` or use the `class` parts.

added: `loader({ ...query, signal })` with `onloaded`, `onerror`, `errorSnippet` and `reload()`.
`pagination`: `pages`, `infinite` (with `onloadmore` when there is no `loader`) or `none`.
`search` bindable, `searchable`, `filterValue` bindable, `filtersProps`, `searchBarProps`, `paginatorProps`, `columnManagerProps`.
`columnManager`: "Columns" button with the `ColumnManager`; `oncolumnstatechange` on save and resize.
Selection bar with "Select all N", `selectionActions` (with `variant: 'danger'` and promises that spin), `selectionDisabled`, `selectionActionsSnippet` for extra content, `selectionBar`, `excluded`.
`pageSizes`, `pageCount`, `rangeSnippet`, `searchSnippet`, `toolbarSnippet`, `labels`, `class` parts (`container`, `toolbar`, `footer`, `selectionBar`, `table`, `header`, `row`, `cell`).
`--data-table-*` variables for the frame, the toolbar, the footer, the messages and the selection bar.
Every prop of `Table`: `expandedSnippet`, `rowHref`, `actionsSnippet`, `actionsVisibility`, cards, `columnState`, `columnsKey`.

manual.summary: Each v4 `Filter` (definition and state in one object) becomes a `FilterField` (definition only) in `fields`.
manual.action: For each object of the v4 `filters` array write a field, keeping the same order: `name`, `label`, `type` (`string` | `number` | `date` | `select` | `bool` | `custom`) and `column` unchanged (`column` now defaults to `name`). `icon`: MDI class → SVG path (global icon transform); `iconColor` has no counterpart (drop it). `tabName` → `category` (the label of the v4 tab, see `multiEditTabs`). `advanced: false` (or absent) with a `mode` (a fixed mode) → `operators: ["<v5 operator>"]` (one operator: the card shows no operator choice); `advanced: true` (the user picked the mode) → omit `operators`, so the field offers the operator set of Filters (`filters-operator-sets`), or list the ones to offer, and set `defaultOperator` to the v5 operator of `mode`. Map `mode` with `filters-modes`. select: `items` keep `{ value, label, icon }` (icon → SVG path), `view: "toggle" | "autocomplete"` unchanged. bool: v4 only filtered on true, so `operators: ["isTrue"]` keeps it; drop `operators` to offer true and false. bool `description` (the v4 checkbox text) → `trueLabel` when it names the true state ("Only active"), otherwise drop it; do not copy it to the field `description`, which is the secondary text in the field list. `betweenModeSingleTextField` → drop (a date `between` always shows one range field). `hidden` did nothing in v4: drop it (v5 `hidden` really hides the field). `multiString` and `choice` were never applied by v4: rewrite them as a `string` field with `columns` or a `select`. `active`, `value`, `values`, `from`, `to` are state: move the applied ones to `value` with `filters-initial-value`; a value set without `active` (it only prefilled the editor) → `defaultValue` on the field, in the v5 shape. `modify` → `filters-modify`; `type: "custom"` → `filters-custom`. Without `operators` a field offers the `standard` set of its type (`filters-operator-sets`), which has more than the v4 modes (string `isNot`, `notContains`; number `ne`, `gte`, `lte`; date `period`, `inLast`; `empty` / `notEmpty` on most types): on apps whose backend is variant E or E' (`global-filter-backends`) pass `operatorSet="basic"` (or `typeOperators`) to Filters to leave out `empty` / `notEmpty`, which those appliers reject. v4 used the filter label as placeholder of the one-edit inputs; v5 shows `labels.value`, `labels.choose` (options) or `labels.search` (`searcher`, `suggest`): give string and select fields a `placeholder` where the app wants its own text. Type the array as `FilterField[]` (`import { type FilterField } from "@likable-hair/svelte"`), keep it out of `$state` unless items change at runtime (then `$derived`), and pass it as `fields`.

manual.summary: v4 `mode` values become v5 operator names, per type.
manual.action: string: `equal` → `is`; `contains` → `contains`; `like` → `like`, `ilike` → `ilike` (same JSON as v4: the value is sent without `%`). On backends that add `%` themselves (variants A–E, see `global-filter-backends`) v4 like/ilike behaved as "contains": prefer `contains` (it sends `ilike "%v%"` with `%` and `_` escaped, same results there); on epass / new-vigipass (no automatic `%`) v4 ilike was a case-insensitive equality: keep `ilike`. number: `equal` → `eq`, `greater` → `gt`, `lower` → `lt`, `between` → `between` (open ends as in v4). date: `equal` → `is` (whole local day, same JSON), `between` → `between` (whole days, same JSON), `lower` → `before` (< start of the day: same results as v4), `greater` → `after`, which is now after the **whole** chosen day (v4 compared the raw midnight value, so the chosen day was included for timestamp columns): use `onOrAfter` to keep including it. Add `dateOnly: true` to fields on `date` columns (no time): the query then compares `yyyy-MM-dd` strings. select: `equal` → `in` (one value: `where(column, "=", v)`; several: `whereIn`; v4 sent a group of `orWhere`), `different` → `notIn` (`<>` or `notWhereIn`). bool `equal` → `isTrue`.

manual.summary: Applied state (`active: true` with `value` / `values` / `from` / `to`) moves from the definitions to the `value` tree.
manual.action: Build the initial tree with `createFilters([...])` and one `filterCondition(name, operator, value)` per v4 filter that had `active: true`: text and number → the value; number between → `{ from, to }` (either may be missing); date → `toISODate(date)` (`"2026-10-09"`), date between → `{ from: toISODate(from), to: toISODate(to) }`; select → the `values` array as it is (`{ value, label }` items; the label is shown in the pill); bool → no value (`filterCondition("paid", "isTrue")`); custom → the value the custom input works with. Operators that v4 did not have (when a `modify` became one): `anyOf` / `noneOf` → an array of strings or numbers; `notBetween` → `{ from, to }`; `inLast`, `inNext`, `olderThan`, `laterThan` → `{ amount: 30, unit: "days" }` (or `30`); `period` → its name (`"thisMonth"`); date fields with `withTime` → `"2026-10-09T14:30"` (`{ from, to }` of those for ranges; `is` / `isNot` stay `yyyy-MM-dd`); `columnEq` … `columnLte` → the `column` of a `compareWith` entry; `match` → the typed text, or `{ value, label }` of a picked suggestion; `empty`, `notEmpty`, `isTrue`, `isFalse` → no value. `let value = $state(createFilters([...]))` and `<Filters {fields} bind:value />`. v4 definitions with a value but without `active` only prefilled the editor: move that value to `defaultValue` on the field (same v5 shape), so a new condition on it starts with it. Constraints the user must not remove → `filterCondition(..., { locked: true })` (also on a `hidden: true` field for invisible ones). Where v4 code built the query from that state (`new FilterConverter().createBuilder({ filters })`), build it with `filtersToBuilder(value, fields)`.

manual.summary: `modify({ builder, value, values, mode })` is gone: declarative field options cover what apps used it for; `apply(builder, condition)` is the fallback.
manual.action: Replace each `modify` by the first option that expresses it: joins to reach the column → `joins: [{ table, on: [from, to] }]` (left join by default, added once and before the conditions) and `column: "table.column"`; `whereIn(key, (q) => q.select(x).from(bridge).where...)` on a bridge table → `through: { key, from: bridge, select: x, joins?, where? }` (an array for several hops; `notIn` / `empty` become `notWhereIn` on the same subquery); OR over several columns, also word by word → string `columns: [...]` + `words: true`; `%v%` added by hand → operator `contains`; `v%` / `%v` → `startsWith` / `endsWith`; a case-sensitive `like` → `caseSensitive: true`; `whereIn` / `notWhereIn` on a list of typed codes or numbers → string or number `anyOf` / `noneOf`; whole-day date ranges written by hand → `between` (built in), their negation → `notBetween`; `whereNull` (also `OR = ""`) → operator `empty` (strings treat `""` as empty by default, `blankIsEmpty`; a bool column that can be null → `nullable: true`); a comparison with another column of the same row (`whereColumn("quantity", "<", "minQuantity")`, `whereColumn("deliveredAt", ">", "promisedAt")`) → on a number or date field `compareWith: [{ column, label }]` (operators `columnEq` … `columnLte`, the user picks the column) or, as a fixed yes / no ("Below minimum"), bool `whenTrue` / `whenFalse` with the `whereColumn`; any other bool that becomes another condition → `whenTrue` / `whenFalse` (they run at every query build, so `new Date()` or app `$state` read inside stay current, and a change of that state re-emits `onchange`); relative dates computed by hand (`new Date()` minus N days: "last 30 days", "older than a year", "next 2 weeks") → date `inLast`, `inNext`, `olderThan`, `laterThan` with `{ amount, unit }` (`FilterRelative`: `days`, `weeks`, `months`, `years`, also `minutes` / `hours` with `withTime`; a plain number = days) or `period` (`today` … `yearToDate`); "valid now" on two date columns → bool `whenTrue: (b) => b.where("validFrom", "<=", new Date()).where("validTo", ">=", new Date())`, or two date conditions `onOrBefore` / `onOrAfter` with `toISODate(new Date())` (fixed when built, e.g. in a preset); a timestamp compared with a date and a time → date `withTime: true` (values `yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm`); a key of a JSONB column (`whereJsonSuperset("customFields", { color: v })`, nested objects) → `json: { column: "customFields", key: "color" }` (dots for nested keys: `"stats.visits"`; the field `column` is not used), only equalities (`is`, `isNot`, `eq`, `ne`, `anyOf`, `noneOf`, `in`, `notIn`, `all`, `isTrue`, `isFalse`); comparisons on a JSON key (`whereRaw("(customFields->>'visits')::numeric > ?")`) → `json: { column, key, cast: "numeric" }` (`text`, `numeric`, `date`, `timestamp`, `boolean`; every operator), which sends `kind: "raw"` and works only on appliers of variant B (on the others the comparison needs a backend change, see `global-filter-backends`); a Postgres array column (`whereRaw("labels && ?")`, `@>`) → select `array: true` (`in` = contains any of, `all` = contains all of, `empty` = null or `{}`); "pick a suggestion (exact match) or keep the typed text (contains)" (addibox `CompanyFilter`, `WarehouseProductFilter`) → string `suggest: ({ searchText, signal }) => items` + `suggestColumn` (column compared with the picked value, default `column`), operator `match` (added first by default); a query applied when the field has no condition ("hide archived" unless asked) → `whenAbsent` (with `operators: ["isTrue"]` and an empty `whenTrue` for "Show archived"); values multiplied (tons → kg) → number `scale` (+ `unit`); one option standing for several values → item `values: [...]`; fixed hidden constraints → `hidden` field + `locked` condition. Only otherwise write `apply: (builder, condition) => { ... }` on the field (it replaces the query of every operator) or an operator definition `{ name, label, input, apply }` in `operators`: read `condition.value` instead of `value` / `values` / `{ from, to }` and `condition.operator` instead of `mode`. Differences: dates arrive as `yyyy-MM-dd` strings (`parseISODate`), selects as `FilterItem[]` (`.map((i) => i.value)`), ranges as `{ from?, to? }`; mutate `builder` and return nothing (a returned builder is ignored, so `return builder.where(...)` still works but `return new FilterBuilder()...` does not). Joins go before the conditions, `orderBy` / `select` / `from` after them (a v4 `modify` that sorted keeps working); a query that mixes `where` and `orWhere` is wrapped in a group, so it never puts an OR at the first level. An operator definition without `apply` uses the field `apply`. Operators outside the `standard` set (`startsWith`, `endsWith`, `anyOf`, `noneOf`, `notBetween`, `onOrBefore`, `onOrAfter`, `inNext`, `olderThan`, `laterThan`) are offered only when listed in the field `operators` or with `operatorSet="all"` (`filters-operator-sets`).

manual.summary: v4 `advanced` (the user picks the mode among those of the type) becomes the operator sets: `operatorSet` on Filters (`basic`, `standard` by default, `all`), `typeOperators` per type, `operators` per field (a list or a set name).
manual.action: Choose the operators for the app, not field by field. Filters that were `advanced: true` stay without `operators` and get `standard` (every v4 mode except `like` / `ilike`, plus `isNot`, `notContains`, `ne`, `gte`, `lte`, `period`, `inLast`, `empty`, `notEmpty`); pass `operatorSet="all"` only where users need every built-in operator (`startsWith`, `endsWith`, `anyOf`, `noneOf`, `notBetween`, `onOrBefore`, `onOrAfter`, `inNext`, `olderThan`, `laterThan`), and `operatorSet="basic"` for simple pages and for backends E / E' (string `contains`, `is`; number `eq`, `between`; date `is`, `between`, `period`; select `in`; no `empty` / `notEmpty`). When the fields of one type need the same list, pass `typeOperators={{ date: ["is", "between", "period"] }}` instead of repeating `operators`; a field `operators` wins over both, as a list (fixed v4 modes stay `operators: ["<operator>"]`) or as a set name (`operators: "all"`). Options still add their operators to any set (`suggest` → `match`, `compareWith` → column operators, `array` / `through` / `json` → `all` outside `basic`, `nullable` → `empty` / `notEmpty`). An operator a rule maps to that is outside the chosen set (`startsWith` for a `v%` modify, `anyOf` for a list of codes) must be listed in `operators` to be offered; in presets, `defaultOperator`, saved filters, the URL or app code any built-in operator of the type works anyway (the card and the panel show it as chosen), except the non-equalities of a `json` key without `cast`, which stay incomplete. A FilterEditor used alone takes the same `operatorSet` and `typeOperators`.

manual.summary: `type: "custom"` filters (value from `customSnippet` + `updateFunction`, query from `modify`) become `type: "custom"` + `apply` + `inputSnippet`, or better a declarative type.
manual.action: First check whether a built-in type does the job (details in `filters-modify`): entity picker with remote search + `whereIn` → `type: "select"` with `searcher: ({ searchText, signal }) => fetch(...)` returning `{ value, label }[]` and `shortcuts: [{ value: me.id, label: "Me" }]` for "assigned to me"; static list → `select` with `items`; countries with flags → `select` with `view: "countries"`; tags of a category with AND/OR → `select` with `through` (operator `all` = has all of, `in` = any of); a Postgres array column → `select` with `array: true`; a free list of codes → string `anyOf` / `noneOf` (outside `standard`: list them in `operators`); "pick a suggestion or keep the typed text" (an Autocomplete that allowed free text) → string `suggest` + `suggestColumn` (operator `match`); missing value → operator `empty`; relative dates ("last 30 days", "valid now") → date `period`, `inLast`, `inNext`, `olderThan`, `laterThan` (`{ amount, unit }`), or bool `whenTrue`; date and time pickers → date `withTime: true`; comparison with another column → `compareWith`; JSONB custom fields → `json: { column, key, cast? }` (equalities without `cast`; with `cast` every operator, backends of variant B only); units → number `unit` + `scale`. Otherwise keep `type: "custom"`, move the v4 `modify` body to `apply: (builder, condition) => { ... }` on the field (see `filters-modify`; without `operators` the field gets the built-in operator `custom`, shown without text), and move the input into one `inputSnippet` on Filters, branching on `field.name`: `{#snippet inputSnippet({ field, value, setValue })}{#if field.name === "x"}<MyInput {value} onchange={(v) => setValue(v)} />{/if}{/snippet}`. Validity: v4 `updateFunction(name, v, valid)` → `setValue(v)`, and the rule that computed `valid` moves to `isComplete: (condition) => ...` on the field (or call `setValue(valid ? v : undefined)`). Without `isComplete` a custom value is complete when it is not `undefined`, `null`, `""`, an empty array or an empty object. The value is plain data in the tree: keep it JSON-serializable. Pills show text and numbers as they are, arrays joined by ", " (items by label) and nothing for objects: give the field `format: (condition) => text` otherwise. Several operators (`is` / `is not`) → `operators: [{ name, label, input: "custom" }]`, read `condition.operator` in `apply`. Remove the app code that reset the custom inputs on remove / remove all: the input reads `value`.

manual.summary: One `onchange({ value, builder })` reloads the data for every change, removals included, and it carries the query; `onremove` and `onopen` are only for side effects.
manual.action: Keep one `onchange` (from `onapplyFilter`) that reloads the data with `e.builder` (the query of the filters, already on top of the `builder` prop): `onchange={({ builder }) => reload(builder)}`. Remove the `FilterConverter` / `Converter` calls inside the old handlers. `e.value` holds only complete conditions. Handlers of `onremoveFilter` / `onremoveAllFilters` that reloaded the data (often the same function) must be deleted, not renamed to `onremove`, or every removal loads twice. To combine with a search or a sort, pass that query as the `builder` prop (Filters re-emits `onchange` when it changes) or call `filtersToBuilder(value, fields, { builder: base })` yourself. `onchange` does not fire on mount: build the first query with `filtersToBuilder(value, fields)` (also in `+page.ts` / `+page.server.ts` load functions). It fires only when the query changes, 300 ms after the last change (`applyDelay`; with `confirm` at Apply), and also when the app changes `value` itself: remove manual reloads that followed a programmatic change, or they run twice. Without `confirm` the user sees the result while editing; add `confirm` only where each query is expensive.

manual.summary: App code that changed the v4 array by hand (`filters[i].active = false`, `filters[i].value = x`, `filters = filters`) works on the tree with helpers now.
manual.action: Rewrite on `value` (a new tree each time; the helpers do not mutate). With `bind:value` assign it; without a bound value Filters keeps its own state, and passing `value={createFilters()}` clears it. Remove all → `value = clearFilters(value)` (keeps `locked`) or `createFilters()`; remove one field → `value = removeFieldConditions(value, "name")`; set or replace one → `value = addFilterNode(removeFieldConditions(value, "name"), filterCondition("name", "is", "x"))`; read a value → `filterConditions(value).find((c) => c.field === "name")?.value`; count → `countFilters(value, fields)`. Items loaded after mount: keep `fields` in a `$derived` (or `$state`) that includes them, or use `searcher`. Saved state (stores, sessionStorage, URL presets, saved views) → see `global-filter-state` (`serializeFilters` / `parseFilters`, `filtersToParam` / `filtersFromParam`, `savable` / `savedKey` / `bind:saved`).

manual.summary: Texts follow `locale` (Italian and English built in) with single texts in one `labels` object (`FilterLabels`), and dates and numbers follow `locale` too. The codemod renames `lang` to `locale` and moves the label props into `labels`.
manual.action: Where the root layout calls `setDefaultLocale("it")`, drop `locale="it"`: it picks every Italian text anyway. Drop `labels` entries that only repeat the default of the language. `labelsMapper` → `labels.operators` (see the `labelsMapper` removal). App wrappers around Filters should set them inside the wrapper.

manual.summary: `appendSnippet` still renders right after the filter buttons; page actions now have their own `actionsSnippet`, pushed to the end of the bar.
manual.action: Most v4 `appendSnippet` contents are page actions ("New", sync, export / import buttons): move them to `actionsSnippet`. Keep `appendSnippet` for content that belongs next to the filters (a count, a toggle). A search field that the app placed before the filters goes in `prependSnippet`.

manual.summary: `customChipSnippet` → `pillSnippet`, which replaces the text of every pill.
manual.action: If the snippet only formatted the value of custom filters, remove it and give those fields `format: (condition) => text` (the pill keeps field and operator; without it arrays show joined by ", " and objects show nothing). Otherwise rename it to `pillSnippet`, render the default text for other fields (`{field.label} {operator} {value}`) and read `condition.value` instead of `filter.value`. Drop the chip markup and the close button from the snippet: the pill keeps its buttons.

manual.summary: New UI: a bar with the "Filters" button (with the count), one pill per condition (field · operator · value, click to edit, × to remove), "+ Add filter" and Clear; the card of one condition; a panel (880px, `--filters-panel-width`) with every condition in rows, where, with `maxDepth`, every filter is a box with "Add nested filter" and the root has one "Add filter"; a bottom sheet up to 1024px. v4 had a button with a dot, chips, menus or a dialog of cards.
manual.action: Check layouts that placed Filters in a row: it now takes 100% of the width (`--filters-width`) and its bar wraps. End-to-end tests: the buttons are "Filters", "Add filter", "Clear" (or the `labels`), pills are buttons named "Edit filter: …", the field list is a listbox, the card a group with radio operators; in the panel each row has "Remove filter" and, with `maxDepth`, "Add nested filter" (there is no "Add group"), and "Add filter" appears once in the bar and once per group (take the last for the root group). Options picked in an Autocomplete show two chips and a "+N" counter (`maxVisibleChips` 2, as in the v4 FilterEditor; 1 in the panel rows); lists of texts or numbers show three chips (two in the rows) and a "+N" button that expands them until "Show less". In the panel rows `view: "toggle"` fields become an Autocomplete when their labels do not fit, and dates show their format as placeholder. A click outside closes only the innermost open menu (an open list inside the panel first, then the panel). App CSS that targeted `.filters-wrapper`, `.filter-button`, `.filter-slot`, `.chip-content`, `.drawer-multi-filter` must use the `aurora-filters-*` classes, `class` parts or `--filters-*` variables.

added: `fields` options: `columns` + `words`, `joins`, `through`, `json` (`{ column, key, cast? }`: a key of a JSONB column; equalities through `whereJsonSuperset`, every operator with `cast` through a parametrized `whereRaw`), `operators` (subset or app-defined), `defaultOperator`, `defaultValue`, `isComplete`, `apply`, `whenAbsent`, `hidden`, `pinned`, `category`, `description`, `format`; string `blankIsEmpty`, `placeholder`, `caseSensitive`, `suggest` + `suggestColumn`; number `unit`, `scale`, `step`, `compareWith`; date `dateOnly`, `periods`, `withTime`, `compareWith`; select `searcher`, `shortcuts`, `view: "countries"`, `locale`, `array` (Postgres array column), item `values`; bool `trueLabel`, `falseLabel`, `whenTrue`, `whenFalse`, `nullable`.

Operator sets instead of v4 `advanced`: `operatorSet` (`basic`, `standard` by default, `all`) and `typeOperators` (a list per type) on Filters and FilterEditor, a set name as field `operators` (`operators: "all"`), `OPERATOR_SETS`, `fieldOperators(field, { set, byType })`; conditions with a built-in operator the field does not offer (presets, URL, saved filters, code) still apply and are shown as chosen.

Text operators ignore case by default, `is` / `isNot` / `anyOf` / `noneOf` included (anchored regex `~*`; v4 sent `=`: add `caseSensitive: true` to keep `=` / `in` and the index). `negativesIncludeEmpty` (Filters, field or `filtersToBuilder`, default `true`) makes the negatives keep the empty rows: it sends `kind: "null"`, so apps on backends E / E' pass `negativesIncludeEmpty={false}`. On relations and arrays `in` / `notIn` read "has any of" / "has none of"; `all` needs `through` or `array`. Operators: string `isNot`, `notContains`, `startsWith`, `endsWith` (Postgres regex `~*`, `~` with `caseSensitive`), `anyOf`, `noneOf`, `match` (with `suggest`), `empty`, `notEmpty`; number `ne`, `gte`, `lte`, `notBetween`, `anyOf`, `noneOf`, `empty`, `notEmpty`; date `isNot`, `onOrBefore`, `onOrAfter`, `notBetween`, `period`, `inLast`, `inNext`, `olderThan`, `laterThan`, `empty`, `notEmpty`; number and date `columnEq`, `columnNe`, `columnGt`, `columnGte`, `columnLt`, `columnLte` (with `compareWith`); select `notIn`, `all` (with `through`, `array` or `json`), `empty`, `notEmpty`; bool `isFalse`, `empty` and `notEmpty` (with `nullable`).

Relative dates take `{ amount, unit }` (`FilterRelative`, units `FilterTimeUnit`: `minutes` and `hours` with `withTime`, `days`, `weeks`, `months`, `years`; a plain number = days); periods `today` … `yearToDate`, with `nextQuarter`, `nextYear`, `monthToDate`, `quarterToDate`, `yearToDate`; date and time values `yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm` with `withTime`.

The same field can appear in several conditions; `allowOr` (AND / OR) and `maxDepth` (nested groups: every filter is a box whose "Add nested filter" turns it into a group or adds a row to it, OR under AND with `allowOr`; one "Add filter" at the root) in the panel.

`pinned` fields always in the bar and `presets` chips (`{ id, label, icon, count, conditions }`), on while every condition of the preset is in the tree (same field, operator and value, however it was added; locked only with locked).

Value inputs with placeholders (`labels.value`, `labels.choose`, `labels.search`, `labels.amount`, or the field `placeholder`) and limited chips (Autocomplete `maxVisibleChips` 2 in the card and 1 in the panel rows; lists of texts or numbers 3 / 2 with a "+N" button and "Show less").

Saved filters: `savable` (a "Saved filters" menu: save the current conditions under a name, apply, delete), `saved` (bindable `SavedFilter[]` `{ id, name, value }`, to keep them in the backend), `savedKey` (keeps them in `localStorage`), `onsavedchange(saved)`.
`confirm` (draft with Cancel / Apply), `applyDelay`, `builder` (base query), `weekStart`, `mobileDrawer`, `class` parts (`container`, `bar`, `pill`, `panel`).
`prependSnippet`, `actionsSnippet`.

Helpers: `createFilters`, `filterCondition`, `filterGroup`, `addFilterNode`, `updateFilterNode`, `removeFilterNode`, `removeFieldConditions`, `clearFilters`, `pruneFilters`, `filterConditions`, `findFilterNode`, `isFilterGroup`, `isConditionComplete`, `countFilters`, `serializeFilters`, `parseFilters`, `filtersToParam` / `filtersFromParam` (the tree in a URL parameter), `filtersToBuilder`, `fieldOperators`, `operatorOf`, `FILTER_OPERATORS`, `OPERATOR_SETS`, `DEFAULT_OPERATORS` (the `standard` set), `DEFAULT_PERIODS`, `filterLabels`, `DEFAULT_FILTER_LABELS`, `FILTER_LABELS_IT`; `FilterBuilder.toQueryParam()`; types `FilterRelative`, `FilterTimeUnit`, `FilterOperatorSet`, `FilterOperatorOptions`, `SavedFilter`.

`labels` texts for the new parts: `units`, `unit`, `addValue`, `addNestedFilter`, `choose`, `search`, `amount`, `showLess`, `time`, `compareWith`, `savedFilters`, `saveFilters`, `saveAs`, `save`, `deleteSaved`, `noSaved`, plus the new operators and periods (all in `FILTER_LABELS_IT`).
`data-count` and `data-open` on the root; `--filters-*` variables for gap, pills, count, "Add filter", connective and panel.

manual.summary: Options can be links now: with `href` the option is an `<a>` (middle click, new tab, SvelteKit preloading) and `currentPath` selects the option whose `href` is the longest match of the page path.
manual.action: Where `onoptionClick` maps `name` to a route with `goto(...)`, put that route in the `href` of each option, pass `currentPath={page.url.pathname}` (from `$app/state`), and delete both the `goto` chain and the code that derives `selected` from the URL. Keep `onoptionClick` only for side effects (closing a drawer is done by SidebarLayout). Do not combine `href` with a `goto`: the page would navigate twice.

manual.summary: A parent without `href` only opens and closes its children: v4 also selected it and called `onoptionClick`.
manual.action: If a parent opened a page in v4 (its name has a route in the app), give it an `href`: it becomes a link with a separate arrow button for the children.

manual.summary: The selected look of v4 was a solid primary pill, v5 a soft gradient with a bar on the left. The codemod removes `--hierarchy-menu-element-selected-background-color` and `-selected-color` set on the menu, so the app takes the v5 look.
manual.action: Look at the menu with a selected option, in light and dark. To restyle it, use `--hierarchy-menu-option-selected-background` and `--hierarchy-menu-option-selected-color` with v5 tokens (`var(--global-color-primary)`).

`data-selected`, `data-ancestor`, `data-open`, `data-depth` on every row, `data-icons-only` on the root.
Every other `--hierarchy-menu-*` variable (icons, indicator, badge, dot, caret, children, flyout).

manual.action: Pass `label` (a visible title above the bar) or `aria-label` saying what the bar measures, and give entries a `label` so the legend reads more than numbers.

renamed.note: The value changes too: v4 took an MDI class name (`name="mdi-plus"`), v5 takes an SVG path on a 24×24 viewBox (`path={mdiPlus}` with `import { mdiPlus } from '@mdi/js'`): apply the global `icons.transform`. A dynamic value (`name={item.icon}`) needs its source converted too. Extra classes inside the v4 value (`"mdi-loading mdi-spin"`) do nothing in v5: see `icon-mdi-helpers`.

removed.name: tabindex
removed.note: Icon is an image and never takes focus. A focusable v4 icon was a clickable one: convert it to a Button (manual step `icon-clickable`).

removed.name: onclick
removed.note: Icon is not clickable (v4 rendered `<span role="button">` even without `onclick`, and called it on any key press). Replace `<Icon name="mdi-x" onclick={f} />` with `<Button buttonType="text" icon={mdiX} aria-label="<what it does>" onclick={f} />`; `variant` sets the color (`secondary` for the text color, `danger` for destructive actions), `size="sm"` makes it smaller. The Button callback receives the native MouseEvent of a `<button>`; v4 passed a MouseEvent or a KeyboardEvent of the `<span>`.
